label: S0200
statement:
EO-MULTICUT-COVER + EO-CUT-RANK (owner derivations 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). seq 17348 closed by owner decision (no follow-up obligation). S_G = Boolean Exact-One solutions of F(G) = proper 3-colourings of G (one-hot x_v, z_{e,c} = 1 - x_{u,c} - x_{w,c}). (A) VERIFIED BY AUTHOR (expansion step accepted as standard): for G' = subdivision of a bounded-degree expander, every representation 1_S = sum_{alpha<=K} f_alpha(x_U) g_alpha(x_U') with nonnegative terms and balanced, term-dependent partitions (triples may be split) needs K = 2^{Omega(d)}: supports are rectangles inside S covering S; a clause split 1|2 makes its singleton coordinate constant on the rectangle; Omega(d) cut clauses give Omega(d) constant coordinates; under the colouring distribution (original vertices uniform, subdivision vertices uniform among allowed colours) every coordinate value has probability <= 2/3 and bounded dependency allows an independent subset J, |J| = Omega(d), so Pr[X in R] <= (2/3)^{|J|}. Consequence: monotone arithmetic circuits for P_G = sum_{x in S} prod X_{i,x_i} need size 2^{Omega(d)} (standard balanced decomposition of cancellation-free set-multilinear computation). Type: multi-partition rectangle cover (DNNF-type / Jerrum-Snir-type monotone bound); to the director's knowledge known technique, novelty of this instance not checked. (B) VERIFIED BY AUTHOR + exhaustive check (48 random splits and edge-triple placements on C4, C5, K4 minus an edge, triangle with tail; rank over GF(1000003) = number of restrictions, 0 mismatches; script scratchpad eo_rank_check.py): for unsplit edge triples, mark for each crossing edge the endpoint opposite to its triple; both sides reconstruct phi on the marked set B and compatibility is exactly agreement on B, so the flattening is block-diagonal with all-ones blocks and rank = |{phi|_B : phi in F_3(G)}| over every field (equal to the rectangle cover number of that cut); minimised over placements = min over vertex covers C of the cut graph of |F_3(G)|_C| (monotone in C); for bipartite G, 2^{nu/2} <= R*_EO <= 3^nu. STRENGTH: membership in S_G is checked clause by clause (AC0, linear size), so neither (A) nor (B) can transfer to Boolean circuit lower bounds; (A) is cancellation-free (monotone) and (B) is exact and tight for one fixed cut (deterministic communication = log of the block count). The arithmetic object P_G (colouring polynomial) points to the general (non-monotone) arithmetic lower-bound problem (VP vs VNP type), not to P != NP. Not a gap closure.

label: S0201
statement:
IPS-SEARCH + CARRY-DICKSON (owner 2026-11-26/27, director check; CLAIMED). (0) Addendum to seq 17359: it omitted THEOREM 14 (seq 5169, full roABP-IPS with bounded placeholder degree), Lemma 15 (seq 5174, placeholder-monomial/width trade-off) and ALG-BIT-001 (seq 3686, 3687, 3727: XOR/carry encoding, degree-2 NS/PC certificates, finite); all are restricted-proof-system or finite results, so the strength map is unchanged. (1) VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: P = NP => PH = P => BPP = P (Sipser-Gacs-Lautemann) => PIT in P => IPS certificates are verifiable in P => the prefix predicate is in P and short IPS refutations are found bit by bit (length by doubling): P = NP => IPS proof search is automatable. This is seq 17136 (E-AUTOMATE, resolution) transferred to IPS. Only one direction is available for IPS ('automatable => P = NP' is Atserias-Mueller for resolution, not known for IPS), so 'IPS is not automatable' is a statement whose truth implies P != NP. 17136(b) applies verbatim: invariants of the certificates themselves (existence, size, annihilators, dual certificates, degree) are unconditional statements that also hold if P = NP, so they cannot bound findability against all algorithms; reductions of the Atserias-Mueller type give the converse direction (automatable => P = NP). BARRIER CHECK (promised for owner step 2): the transfer relativises (and algebrises), so a proof of non-automatability needs a non-relativising and non-algebrising step; no candidate step is named. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (extends 17136): invariant-based limits on IPS proof search as a route to P != NP. (2) CARRY-DICKSON, VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: XOR part solved by Gaussian elimination (x = x0 + By), carry equations become quadratics q_j; reducing modulo the span of their quadratic parts leaves r quadratic plus affine equations; Z = 2^{-r} sum_lambda sum_y (-1)^{lambda.q(y)}, each inner sum 0 or +-2^{e-k_lambda} by Dickson, computable in poly time; hence exact counting/decision in 2^r poly(|F|). Classical (Dickson/Arf; counting solutions of r quadratic equations over F_2 in 2^r poly time); the Dickson character sums were already used in the book (seq 846, 3973, 4020). It is an algorithm, i.e. an upper bound; for an NP-complete family r cannot be O(log n) on all instances unless P = NP, which is not provable here. Not a gap closure.

label: S0202
statement:
INTERVAL-LINEARISATION (owner 2026-11-27, director check; CLAIMED, needs review by another model family). Setting: full roABP-IPS refutation C(x,y) of Psi_n (axioms = clause products Q_j of literal indicators, placeholders y_j), width w in a total order pi of x and y; I_j = span in pi of {y_j} union vars(Q_j); N = placeholders occurring in a monomial with another placeholder or with degree >= 2; p_N = max over cuts of #{j in N : I_j crosses the cut} (p_N <= owner's p). CLAIM: Psi_n has an roABP-IPS_LIN refutation (functional form, Boolean-axiom terms free) of width <= 1 + m w 2^{p_N} in the induced x-order; with Theorem 12 (seq 5128): log2 w + p_N >= c1 n - O(log m), c1 = Theorem 12 exponent constant (not explicit). PROOF. (A) Telescoping: C(x,Q) - C(x,0) = sum_j [C(Q_<j,1,0_>j) - C(Q_<j,0,0_>j)] Q_j =: sum_j Q_j D_j pointwise on the cube, since Q_j in {0,1} there; so sum_j Q_j D_j = 1 on the cube. For j not in N, D_j = coefficient g_j(x) of y_j, width <= w (coefficient extraction, as Lemma 15 (i), seq 5174). For j in N only placeholders in N are substituted. (B) Cut rank: at a pi-cut write C = sum_{k<=w} A_k(x_L,y_L) B_k(x_R,y_R). For y_i on the left with I_i crossing, Q_i = L_i(x_L) R_i(x_R) (on the cube); Moebius expansion in the Boolean values gives A_k(x_L,Q) = sum_{T subset S_L} alpha_{k,T}(x_L) prod_{i in T} L_i prod_{i in T} R_i, each term rank 1; same for B_k. Non-crossing placeholders are one-sided functions (no cost). Hence cube-evaluation rank of D_j at the cut <= w 2^{p_N}. ml(D_j) has coefficient-matrix rank = cube-evaluation rank (Kronecker product of invertible 2x2 transforms, every field), so ml(D_j) is an roABP of width <= w 2^{p_N} in the induced order (Nisan). (C) sum_j Q_j ml(D_j) - 1 vanishes on the cube, hence lies in the Boolean ideal. Theorem 12 is functional: Lemma T (report l.268-274) uses only 'on the cube the Boolean-axiom terms vanish' and the cube rank of a_D at a cut, so the Boolean quotients h need no width bound. REVIEW POINT: check that Lemma O (order reduction, report l.323-346) is likewise only a restriction of the a_D (functional), so Theorem 12 applies to cube-rank widths. STRENGTH/REDUNDANCY: incomparable with Theorem 14 (placeholder degree <= c' n, seq 5169) and Lemma 15 (t placeholder monomials, seq 5174); covers part of the Theorem 14 remainder (degree > c' n with nonlinear placeholders spread so few cross any cut). Not covered: certificates with >= c1 n - log(mw) nonlinear placeholders crossing some cut; Theorem 16 (seq 5192) shows every order has a cut crossed by K = Omega(n) disjoint clauses, so the canonical product certificate has p_N = Omega(n) and the bound is vacuous there (Theorem 16 handles it). CLAIM: Psi_n has an roABP-IPS_LIN refutation (functional form, Boolean-axiom terms free) of width <= 1 + m w 2^{p_N} in the induced x-order; with Theorem 12 (seq 5128): log2 w + p_N >= c1 n - O(log m), c1 = Theorem 12 exponent constant (not explicit). PROOF. (A) Telescoping: C(x,Q) - C(x,0) = sum_j [C(Q_<j,1,0_>j) - C(Q_<j,0,0_>j)] Q_j =: sum_j Q_j D_j pointwise on the cube, since Q_j in {0,1} there; so sum_j Q_j D_j = 1 on the cube. For j not in N, D_j = coefficient g_j(x) of y_j, width <= w (coefficient extraction, as Lemma 15 (i), seq 5174). For j in N only placeholders in N are substituted. (B) Cut rank: at a pi-cut write C = sum_{k<=w} A_k(x_L,y_L) B_k(x_R,y_R). (C) sum_j Q_j ml(D_j) - 1 vanishes on the cube, hence lies in the Boolean ideal. statement:
MATROID-CUT-RANK for P_B (owner derivation 2026-11-27, director check; CLAIMED, needs review by another model family). (T1) Field F, P(u,v) = prod_i (a_i(u) + b_i(v) + c_i)^2, no factor the zero polynomial. If M (|M| = m) has {a_i}_M and {b_i}_M both linearly independent, then rank_{u|v}(P) >= 2^m (formal coefficient rank). Check: u_s with a_i(u_s) = t_i + s_i d_i, v_r with b_i(v_r) = -t_i - c_i - (1 - r_i) d_i; selected factor = (s_i + r_i - 1) d_i, so P(u_s, v_r) = 0 for s != r. Diagonal: every other factor is a nonzero polynomial in (t, d, free coordinates) (if a_j, b_j lie in the spans with coefficients lambda, mu, identical vanishing forces lambda = mu and lambda_i (2 s_i - 1) = 0, hence a_j = b_j = 0 and the factor is the nonzero constant c_j^2); the product of all diagonal factors and all d_i is a nonzero polynomial, so a good point exists over an infinite field. Over F_3 take an extension field: coefficient-matrix rank is invariant under field extension, and evaluation rank <= coefficient rank. Correct. Same mechanism as Lemma M9b' (seq 5192: diagonal evaluation + generic avoidance of the other factors); new is independence in place of variable-disjointness. (T2) Upper bound: with Edmonds' partition J (a = rk B_L[J], b = rk B_R[I \ J]), rank <= (D+1)^{a+b}; hence 2^kappa <= rank <= (D+1)^kappa, kappa = matroid-intersection number of the two row matroids at the cut. Correct. (T3) Application to K_G (q = 3, dim 2|V|), any basis B, any order pi, p = max over prefix cuts of kappa: for every vertex set S (h = |S|) a prefix cut with dim pi_S(L) = h exists; L' = {l in L : l|_J = 0}, R' = {r in R : r|_{I \ J} = 0}; S_L and S_R are disjoint (two nonzero vectors with coordinate sum 0 in F_3^3 share a support coordinate) and non-adjacent (if v in S_L, w in S_R then L'|_w = 0 and R'|_v = 0, so z_e = -x_v resp. -x_w have >= 2 of 3 nonzero edge coordinates on opposite sides of J: contradiction); |S_L| >= (h-a)/2, |S_R| >= (h-b)/2, separator D = S minus (S_L u S_R) with |D| <= p/2. Correct. CORRECTION (constant): components can still be (h+p)/2 > h/2, while Dvorak-Norin (from memory: every subgraph has a separator leaving components <= |V(H)|/2, of order k => tw <= 15k; verify at source) needs 1/2-balance. One more round on the large component (h >= 3p), else remove ceil(h/2) <= 1.5p vertices, gives order <= 1.5p, so tw(G) <= 22.5 p; the claim tw <= 15 p is not proved as written. RESULT (CLAIMED): min over kernel bases B and orders pi of the formal roABP width of P_B >= 2^{tw(G)/23} (Nisan: width = max prefix coefficient rank). STRENGTH: an unconditional lower bound for 'roABP after an invertible linear change of variables' on one explicit product of squared affine forms; P_B has small depth-3 circuits. w* = 2 tw + 1 (seq 4079) is NOT used in the proof; writing 2^{(w*-1)/46} is substitution only. The shared ingredient is the support lemma of the w* lower bound (seq 4071). Not related to M9 (IPS certificates of Psi_n). Literature novelty of T1/T2 (rank of products of linear forms vs matroid intersection) not checked. No consequence for P != NP.

label: S0204
statement:
REVIEW TARGET W-STAR (owner request 2026-11-27: definition fidelity + novelty; CLAIMED until reviewed by a NON-Claude model family). THEOREM: G finite simple, I = (V x {1,2,3}) u (E x {1,2,3}), K_G subset GF(3)^I given by sum_c k(v,c) = 0 and k(e,c) = -(k(u,c) + k(w,c)) for e = uw; dim K_G = 2|V|. For a basis B = (b_j) of K_G let H_B be the graph on basis indices with j ~ k iff some coordinate i has b_j(i) != 0 and b_k(i) != 0. Then min_B tw(H_B) = 2 tw(G) + 1. Lower bound (proof-state Q-5f55fb62c2:S0009): (L1) nonzero t in GF(3)^3 with sum 0 has >= 2 nonzero entries; (L2) two subsets of {1,2,3} of size >= 2 meet; (i) S_v = {j : b_j nonzero on block v} is a clique; (ii) S_u u S_w is a clique for each edge; (iii) |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X| (projection onto T^X is surjective); (iv) from a width-w decomposition of H_B, beta_G(t) = {v : S_v subset beta(t)} is a decomposition of G (Helly), so w >= 2 tw(G) + 1. Upper bound (S0012): natural basis has H_B = G[K_2], tw(G[K_2]) <= 2 tw(G) + 1. Lean 4.35 + Mathlib, kernel-checked (seq 4079, build audit seq 8730), public sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tonnestate/FruitStack-Eval/332a3ffeaaf6cd5ed6443fa8e3a004210fec54f4/results/PNP-001-research-graph-export/reviews/formal/wstar/WStarLower.lean (sha256 prefix dbfc812c176fae4b), https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tonnestate/FruitStack-Eval/332a3ffeaaf6cd5ed6443fa8e3a004210fec54f4/results/PNP-001-research-graph-export/reviews/formal/wstar/WStar.lean, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tonnestate/FruitStack-Eval/332a3ffeaaf6cd5ed6443fa8e3a004210fec54f4/results/PNP-001-research-graph-export/reviews/formal/wstar/Blowup.lean. REVIEW TASKS: (F) fidelity - do Ker, coeffGraph, TwLe and the statements tw_le_of_coeff_tw, wstar_le_two_tw_add_one, wstar_eq_iff encode exactly this theorem (the previous lab attempts R1293/R1325 could not read the Lean source; it is now public at the URLs above); (P) proof - check S0009 (i)-(iv); the only prior review (R1319) was the same model family as the author. (N) novelty - search for prior statements of: minimum over bases of a linear code/subspace of the treewidth of the support-intersection graph; treewidth of linear-algebraic reparametrisations of k-colouring; tw(G[K_n]) = n(tw(G)+1) - 1. Scope: the 3-colouring kernel F(G) only; says nothing about nonlinear reparametrisations or other algorithms (seq 17391).

statement:
SUBSPACE SIEVE for positive 1-in-3 SAT (owner 2026-11-27; owner proof, PI re-derivation and check; CLAIMED, Claude family only). Setup: weighted T41 matrix B(X) over char 2, joint Schur (17432): K = [[A,D],[D^T,0]] on T u R, |R| = nu. (1) rank D < nu => unsatisfiable. (2) Q = basis of the left kernel of D (|T| x r, r = |T|-nu), C = Q^T A Q, q_i = rows of Q. K_U invertible <=> [[C,Q_U^T],[Q_U,0]] invertible (both <=> rank Q_U = |U| and C nondegenerate on ker Q_U). Consequences: h with dependent rows q_i (i in E_h) is never true; h,g whose row spans do not form a direct sum are never true together (this also encodes E_h disjointness). (3) Char 2: det[[C,L^T],[L,0]] = sum_{|I|=k} det(L[:,I])^2 det C[complement of I]; hence with W = span of admissible rows, s = dim W, a basis change putting W on y_1..y_s: F satisfiable <=> Z(lambda) = [y_1...y_s] sqrt(det(J_s + Y'CY')) prod_h (1 + lambda_h prod_{i in E_h} l_i(y)) is nonzero. (4) Algorithm: random weights and lambda in a polynomial-size field of char 2, coefficient by sum over 2^s subsets plus interpolation in t; time O*(2^s), polynomial space, one-sided error <= (m+|H|)/|F| (only one satisfying selection must survive). Portfolio O*(2^{min(|H|, s, d)}), d = F_3 nullity of the clause matrix (algorithm R). Check: sieve_check.py, 90 random instances (occurrences <= 4): algorithm = brute force 90/90, no false positive or negative, direct formula 90/90; s < |H| in 2/90. Placement: instance of determinantal sieving (Eiben-Koana-Wahlstroem arXiv 2502.13654 Thm 5, O*(2^r), char 2) adapted to symmetric matrices with diagonal; novelty of the parameter s unchecked. Extreme case every variable exactly 3 times: B=0, nu=0, C=0, s=m=n (RX3C, NP-complete): no saving. Random RX3C: F_3 nullity 1-3 in 600/600 (n=30,60,120). No lower bound, no P vs NP statement.

label: S0209
statement:
KEMPE SPACE of F(G) (owner 2026-11-27; owner proofs, PI re-derivation and check kempe_check.py; CLAIMED, Claude family only). (1) W_G = span_Q of b_K = 1_{K cap V_a} - 1_{K cap V_b} over all 3-colourings and all bichromatic components K. dim aff(Sol01(F(G))) = 2 dim W_G. Proof: a Kempe swap changes x by b_K (x) (e_b - e_a); colour permutations give b_K (x) U, U = sum-zero subspace of Q^3, dim 2; conversely the average of the 6 colour permutations of a colouring is (1/3)1(x)1, and x_chi - (1/3)1(x)1 = (1_{V1}-1_{V3})(x)f1 + (1_{V2}-1_{V3})(x)f2 with 1_{Va}-1_{Vb} a sum of b_K; so the direction space is W_G (x) U. (Edge auxiliaries are affine in x.) Checked: prism, K33, C5, a 7-vertex graph: equality 4/4. Prism: 2 Kempe classes, dim W per class 2 and 2, total 4. (2) Frozen pair (owner): G_phi from (not t) or phi via (not t or a or p)(not p or b or c), a or b or c <=> exists z NAE(a,b,z), NAE(not z,c,0), NAE = triangle gadget; G_phi always 3-colourable with a colouring computable from t = false; phi UNSAT <=> col(t) = col(F) in every colouring <=> x_{t,1} - x_{f,1} = 0 on aff(Sol01(F(G_phi))) (colour symmetry). Hence computing the affine hull, even given a solution, is in P iff P = NP (forward direction: P = NP lets one extend the hull by search, at most N rounds). (3) Unit-vector membership: with p, q adjacent to t and T: phi SAT <=> e_p in W_{G_phi}; NP-complete (certificate <= N Kempe vectors, Gauss), even with a supplied colouring and deg(p) = 2. Gadget checked both ways on a 6-vertex model. Strength: (2) and (3) are reductions, i.e. equivalent reformulations of NP-hardness (frozen pairs are a known concept); (1) is an exact structural identity.

label: S0210
statement:
MIS GENERATORS OF THE KEMPE SPACE (owner 2026-11-27; PI check mis_span_check.py: 255 random graphs n<=8, rank W = rank gens = rank union, 0 mismatches; CLAIMED, Claude family only). G 3-colourable; I_G = {I independent, G-I bipartite}; M_G = inclusion-maximal members (= maximal independent sets of G with bipartite complement); R_G = {v: exists M in M_G, v in M, M-v in I_G}. THEOREM: W_G = span_Q({3*1_M - 1 : M in M_G} u {e_v : v in R_G}). PROOF: (a) W_G = span{3*1_I - 1 : I in I_G}: every I in I_G is a colour class (2-colour G-I); for classes A,B,C of a colouring 3*1_A-1 = (1_A-1_B)+(1_A-1_C), each a sum of Kempe vectors b_K; conversely b_K = 1_{K cap A}-1_{K cap B} = 1_A - 1_{A'} with A' the class after the swap, = ((3*1_A-1)-(3*1_{A'}-1))/3. (b) For I in I_G extend to a maximal independent M; G-M is an induced subgraph of G-I, so M in M_G; for v in M-I, M-v contains I, so M-v in I_G and v in R_G; 3*1_I-1 = (3*1_M-1) - 3*sum_{v in M-I} e_v. (c) 3e_v = (3*1_M-1)-(3*1_{M-v}-1) for v in R_G. QED. ALGORITHM: enumerate maximal independent sets with polynomial delay and polynomial space (Tsukiyama et al. 1977, from memory, verify at source), at most 3^{n/3} (Moon-Moser 1965); test bipartiteness of G-M and of G-(M-v); keep an incremental Q-basis (<= n vectors, Bareiss). With one colouring from any M in M_G, aff(Sol01(F(G))) = x_chi + W_G (x) U (17497). Time O*(3^{n/3}) = O*(1.4423^n), polynomial space. STRENGTH: exponential upper bound only; same enumeration as Lawler's 1976 3-colouring algorithm (from memory, verify), here lifted to the span. Hull computation is NP-hard (17497 (2)), so no polynomial version is expected. No lower bound, no obligation closed, no P vs NP progress.

label: S0212
statement:
CONSTANT-TEMPERATURE CORRELATION AMPLIFIER (owner 2026-11-27; PI check of every bound; exact M^3 by fractions; CLAIMED, Claude family). Input: G_phi from the switch-vertex construction (17497/17506), always 3-colourable, n vertices, with a pair (u,v) such that phi in SAT iff some proper colouring has sigma(u) = sigma(v) (the pair (t,T) of 17497 (3)). STEP A: add r = 2n+3 new vertices, each adjacent to u and v. Then Z(0) = 2^r A + B (A, B = colourings with equal or different colours at u, v; A+B <= 3^n). UNSAT: A = 0, so p_r = 0. SAT: p_r >= 2^r/(2^r+3^n) >= 8/9, since 2^{2n+3} >= 8*3^n. STEP B: T = 1/ln 2, so the conflict weight is 1/2 and M = J - I/2. M^3 = (1/8)[[41,42,42],...] (eigenvalues 125/8 and -1/8); M^2 has ratio 9/8 > 1, so an odd length is required. Replace each of the |E| edges of the N-vertex amplified graph by k = 42(2N+4) internally disjoint paths of length 3. The marginal on the original vertices is then proportional to q^{H(tau)} with q = (41/42)^k <= e^{-(2N+4)}. Proper colourings exist, so the conflict mass is <= 3^N q < 0.0075 < 1/16. RESULT: UNSAT gives P(sigma(u)=sigma(v)) <= 1/16; SAT gives >= (15/16)(8/9) = 5/6. The graph has size O(|E| N k) = poly(n). Hence approximating this two-point correlation at fixed T within additive error < 37/96 is NP-hard under polynomial-time many-one reductions. STRENGTH: relative hardness only, with unbounded degree. Known-type: inapproximability of the antiferromagnetic Potts model beyond uniqueness, already for bounded degree (Galanis-Stefankovic-Vigoda; from memory, verify), is stronger. No unconditional lower bound and no obligation closed.

Input: G_phi from the switch-vertex construction (17497/17506), always 3-colourable, n vertices, with a pair (u,v) such that phi in SAT iff some proper colouring has sigma(u) = sigma(v) (the pair (t,T) of 17497 (3)). STEP A: add r = 2n+3 new vertices, each adjacent to u and v. Then Z(0) = 2^r A + B (A, B = colourings with equal or different colours at u, v; A+B <= 3^n). UNSAT: A = 0, so p_r = 0. SAT: p_r >= 2^r/(2^r+3^n) >= 8/9, since 2^{2n+3} >= 8*3^n. STEP B: T = 1/ln 2, so the conflict weight is 1/2 and M = J - I/2. Replace each of the |E| edges of the N-vertex amplified graph by k = 42(2N+4) internally disjoint paths of length 3. The marginal on the original vertices is then proportional to q^{H(tau)} with q = (41/42)^k <= e^{-(2N+4)}. Proper colourings exist, so the conflict mass is <= 3^N q < 0.0075 < 1/16. RESULT: UNSAT gives P(sigma(u)=sigma(v)) <= 1/16; SAT gives >= (15/16)(8/9) = 5/6. The graph has size O(|E| N k) = poly(n). (3) Weighted removal: Q_G(X) = sum over proper sigma of prod_v X_{v,sigma(v)}. Char != 2: weight 1/2 on one internal vertex per gadget. Char 2: over F_4 with omega^2 + omega + 1 = 0, weights v1 (1,1,1), v2 (omega,omega^2,1), v3 (omega^2,omega,1); the gadget sum is 1 on NAE inputs and 0 otherwise, verified 8/8 for all 6 choices of reference colours. (4) Projection: take the parsimonious tableau 3-CNF Psi_n of the clocked machine (branch choice recorded, idle padding, Tseitin auxiliaries determined; 17548) with free inputs x. Set G_n = colouring graph of Psi_n and let pi be: reference vertices X_{ref,c} = [c = designated colour] (removes the factor 6); positive literal vertex of x_i: X_{T} = X_{i,1}, X_{F} = X_{i,0}, X_{B} = 0; gadget weights as in (3); every other variable 1. Then pi(Q_{G_n}) = sum_x U_n(x) prod_i X_{i,x_i} = P_n over every field K with char K != 2 or omega in K. For char 2 without omega: size_K(Q) >= size_{K(omega)}(Q) >= size_{K(omega)}(P_n). Size |G_n| = O(|Psi_n|) = O(T^2), T = n^{10^9}. Weights X_{v,c} on x_{v,c} and 1 on y give Gen_{F(G)} = Q_G, coefficient by coefficient; hence P_n = pi(Gen_{F(G_n)}). =p then ceil(a/p)=(a+p-1)/p < 2a/p = 2max(a/p,1). Hence max(a/p,1) <= ceil(a/p) < 2max(a/p,1), the right inequality being strict and sup = 2 approached at a=p+1 (ratio 2p/(p+1) -> 2), so no constant c<2 works uniformly. Multiplying over j=1..J and summing over alpha gives T <= K' <= 2^J T with T := sum_alpha prod_j max(a_{alpha,j}/p,1); since prod_j max(a/p,1) = W_alpha 2^{-Phi_h(alpha)} with W_alpha = prod_j a_{alpha,j}, T is the W-weighted expectation W*E_X[2^{-Phi_h}] (X ~ W_alpha/W), NOT the uniform A*E_X[2^{-Phi_h}] written in S0194 - under the uniform reading the claimed identity fails a second time. Exactness: K' = T * prod_j r_{alpha,j} with r in [1,2), so K' >= T always (this is the surviving direction, and ceil>=1 gives K' >= K_acc). Consequence: log2(w'K') <= log2 w' + log2 T + J, whereas S0194 (3) needs log2(w'K') <= h+1+log2 A - P(h); the two agree only if J <= h+1+log2 A - P(h) - log2 w' - log2 T, which fails in the many-block regime, so consequence (3) as stated is dead and only (1),(2),(4),(5) (which use K' >= K_acc) survive. (=>) If f(beta) > 0 for some beta in (0,1], then max(A, A-D) >= f(beta) > 0, so A > 0 or A-D > 0. statement: Lemma: For all real c ≥ 1, η ∈ [0,1), k ≥ 0, and β ∈ (0,1], the inequality (2+β-η)/(1+c) > 1+kβ holds iff 3-η > (1+k)(1+c). Proof: The expression is linear in β. For fixed c,η,k, define f(β) = (2+β-η)/(1+c) - (1+kβ). Then f(β) = (1-c-η)/(1+c) + β(1/(1+c) - k). Since c ≥ 1 and η ≥ 0, 1-c-η ≤ 0, so f(0+) ≤ 0. The inequality f(β) > 0 can only hold if the coefficient of β is positive, i.e., 1/(1+c) > k, and f(1) > 0. f(1) = (3-η)/(1+c) - (1+k) = (3-η - (1+k)(1+c))/(1+c). Since 1+c > 0, f(1) > 0 iff 3-η > (1+k)(1+c). If 1/(1+c) ≤ k, then f is non-increasing and f(β) ≤ f(0+) ≤ 0 for all β ∈ (0,1], so the inequality never holds; in this case 3-η ≤ 3 ≤ (1+k)(1+c) since k ≥ 1/(1+c) implies (1+k)(1+c) ≥ (1+1/(1+c))(1+c) = 2+c ≥ 3. Thus the equivalence holds exactly as stated.

statement: For every n and every language slice L_n subseteq {0,1}^n with |L_n| <= S(n), there is a Boolean circuit C_n deciding L_n of size O(S(n)n). Proof: enumerate L_n as y_1,...,y_t, t<=S(n). For each y_i build the conjunction of n literals asserting x=y_i, using O(n) fan-in-2 gates; OR the t equality tests using O(t) gates. This circuit accepts exactly the listed strings, hence exactly L_n. For t=0 use the constant-zero circuit. Therefore if S(n) is polynomial, L is in P/poly by taking C_n as length-n advice-selected circuit; if S(n)=2^{n^beta}, this bound is exponential and does not imply P/poly.

statement:
statement: Let G be a connected graph, c: V -> {0,1} with sum_v c(v) odd, and Tseitin(G,c) the GF(2) CNF on edge variables that contains, for each vertex v, every clause excluding one parity-violating assignment of the edges at v. Then every resolution refutation of Tseitin(G,c) contains a clause of width >= min{deg(v) : c(v) = 1}. Corollary: for K_n with c(0)=1 and c(v)=0 otherwise (n odd-sum parity fixed), every refutation has width >= n-1, so refutation width is unbounded in n for this encoding.
derivation: Let x = 0. For a vertex v with c(v)=0, the parity of x at v is even, so no clause of v's parity-violating family is falsified by x: every such clause is satisfied by x. For a vertex v with c(v)=1 and deg(v)=d, x has even parity at v, so the single clause of v's family that excludes x|_{edges at v} is falsified by x; that clause has width d. Let w < min{deg(v): c(v)=1}. Then every initial clause of width <= w is satisfied by x (clauses of charge-0 vertices by the parity argument, and charge-1 clauses have width >= min deg > w so they are absent). Resolution is sound: if C and D are satisfied by a fixed assignment x, every resolvent of C and D is satisfied by x. Hence every clause derivable with width <= w is satisfied by x, and the empty clause, which x does not satisfy, is not derivable. So no refutation of width <= w exists, i.e. every refutation has a clause of width >= min odd-charge degree. Check on bowtie (deg 4 at vertex 0): width >= 4 (matches measured minimal width 4 in cm-5e55529b375c468f, so tw+1 = 3 is refuted for this encoding). K_n with one odd vertex: width >= n-1 (measured K4: 4 >= 3; K5: >= 7 >= 4, so the bound is not tight there).
scope: Gf(2) Tseitin CNF with edge variables and all parity-violating clauses per vertex, as stated. Does not cover the GF(3) kernel encoding F(K_n) of Q-33e33ccf08 or any other encoding. Lower bound only; no upper bound claimed.

label: S0004
statement:
statement: Let F be an unsatisfiable CNF over Boolean variables and let x be any assignment. Let m(x) = min{|C| : C in F and x falsifies C} (m(x) = infinity if x falsifies no clause). Then every resolution refutation of F contains a clause of width >= m(x). Corollary: if some x falsifies only clauses of width >= m, then F has no refutation of width < m. The degree lemma S0003 is the special case F = Tseitin(G,c), x = 0.
derivation: Let P be a resolution refutation of F and suppose every clause of P has width < m(x). Each initial clause of P is a clause of F with width < m(x), so by definition of m(x) x satisfies it. Resolution is sound for a fixed assignment: if clauses C and D are both satisfied by x, a resolvent of C and D is satisfied by x, because the resolved variable is satisfied by x via one of C or D. By induction every clause of P is satisfied by x. The last clause of P is the empty clause, which x does not satisfy. Contradiction. Hence P contains a clause of width >= m(x). The corollary follows by taking x that falsifies only clauses of width >= m. Check: for x = 0 and Tseitin(G,c) with c(v)=1 at vertex v, m(0) = min odd-charge degree, which recovers S0003.
scope: Any unsatisfiable CNF F and any assignment x, resolution (Boolean, no weakening, width = max clause size in the refutation). Gives only a lower bound; it does not give an upper bound. It does not by itself say anything about the GF(3) kernel encoding of F(K_n) or about Search-MCSP. Its use for part (A) requires exhibiting, for a given CNF encoding of F(K_n), an x whose falsified clauses are all wide; that check is not done here.

statement: statement: For every m>=1 and every nonempty A subseteq {0,1}^m, the indicator of A has a fan-in-2 AND/OR circuit with free input negations and at most sum_{d=2}^m |P_d(A)| + |A|-1 gates, where P_d(A) is the set of length-d prefixes of strings in A. Proof: for each distinct prefix u of length d>=2, compute its conjunction from the conjunction for its length-(d-1) parent and the literal at position d, using one binary AND gate; length-1 prefixes are literals and require no gates. The resulting length-m conjunctions are precisely the minterms for A. OR the |A| minterms using |A|-1 binary OR gates. The total is the stated bound. This refines the independent-minterm bound when prefixes are shared; it is only an upper bound for this construction, not a lower bound for general circuits.

statement: statement: Cofactor sparsity lemma. Let m>=k>=0, let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^m of size t, and let I be any set of k coordinates. For each assignment b in {0,1}^I let A_b={x in A:x|_I=b}. Then some b has |A_b|<=floor(t/2^k). If this cofactor is nonempty, its indicator on the remaining m-k coordinates has a fan-in-2 AND/OR circuit with free input negations of size at most floor(t/2^k)(m-k)-1; if it is empty, its indicator is the constant 0 and needs no gates. Proof: the 2^k fibers A_b partition A, so their integer sizes sum to t; if all exceeded floor(t/2^k), their sum would exceed t. For a nonempty chosen fiber of size u, apply the minterm construction: u minterms each use m-k-1 AND gates and their OR uses u-1 gates, total u(m-k)-1, which is at most floor(t/2^k)(m-k)-1. The empty case is represented by constant 0. This gives a small cofactor only; it does not imply a small circuit for the original function or a gate-elimination lower bound.

statement: statement: For every m>=2, every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with exactly two accepting inputs has a fan-in-2 AND/OR circuit of at most 2m-1 gates when input negations are free; hence for every real c>=2 and integer m>=2, every such f belongs to MCSP[m^c]. Proof: write the two accepting inputs as a,b. For each, form its full minterm using m-1 binary AND gates (literals and their negations are free); OR the two minterms with one binary OR gate. The total is 2(m-1)+1=2m-1. Since 2m-1<=m^2<=m^c for m>=2 and c>=2, the membership follows. statement: statement: Cofactor-decomposition upper bound. Let m>=1, 0<=k<=m, and let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have nonempty support A of size t. Fix any set I of k input coordinates, and let q be the number of assignments b in {0,1}^I for which the fiber A_b={x in A:x|_I=b} is nonempty. In the fan-in-2 AND/OR basis with free input negations and constants available, f has a circuit with at most t(m-k)+qk-1 gates. Proof: For each nonempty fiber b, form its selector conjunction on I, using k-1 AND gates when k>=1 (for k=0 the selector is the constant 1 and costs zero). On the remaining m-k variables, write the fiber indicator as the OR of its u_b minterms, where u_b=|A_b|; this takes u_b(m-k)-1 gates when m-k>=1. If m-k=0, each nonempty residual fiber is the constant 1 and takes zero gates; the same expression u_b(m-k)-1 is then not used as a literal gate count. Combine selector and residual indicator with one AND gate when both are nonconstant; if either is constant 1, omit that gate, and if the selector is constant 1 use the residual indicator directly. Finally OR the q resulting fiber terms with q-1 gates. For k,m-k>=1 the total is sum_b[u_b(m-k)-1]+q(k-1)+q+(q-1)=t(m-k)+qk-1. If k=0, q=1 and the ordinary support DNF uses tm-1 gates, agreeing with the bound. If k=m, each fiber is a singleton selector and their OR costs q(m-1)+(q-1)=qm-1, also agreeing with the bound. Thus the bound holds in all boundary cases. This is an explicit upper bound for a selected decomposition, not a lower bound for general circuits or a gate-elimination result.

statement: Circuit-description counting lemma. Fix m,s>=1 and the fan-in-2 Boolean circuit model with m input wires, gates of types AND, OR, NOT, constants available, and one designated output wire. The number of circuits with at most s gates is at most (s+1)(m+s) [3(m+s)^2]^s. Indeed, encode a circuit by its gate count j<=s, then for each gate choose one of at most 3 types and at most (m+s)^2 predecessor choices (this overcounts NOT and constant gates), and choose the output among at most m+s wires. Summing over j gives at most (s+1)(m+s)[3(m+s)^2]^s. Consequently the fraction of m-bit Boolean functions computable by such circuits is at most (s+1)(m+s)[3(m+s)^2]^s/2^(2^m). This bound concerns circuit density only; it supplies no local cofactor classification or gate-elimination estimate for MCSP[m^c].
proof: The encoding overcounts because it allows choices of wires that may not be valid predecessors and treats all gate types as having two inputs. Every valid circuit nevertheless has at least one encoding among these descriptions. Thus the number of circuits is bounded by the number of descriptions. There are at most s+1 choices of gate count, at most 3(m+s)^2 choices per gate, and at most m+s choices of output. Divide this bound by the 2^(2^m) Boolean functions to obtain the density bound.

statement_start: Cofactor tail bound. Let m>=k>=0, I be any k coordinates of {0,1}^m, and A⊆{0,1}^m have size t. For q>=0, at most floor(t/(q+1)) assignments b to I have |A_b|>q.
evidence: Proof: The fibers A_b={x∈A:x|_I=b} are disjoint and partition A, so their sizes sum to t. If r fibers have more than q elements, each has at least q+1, hence t≥r(q+1) and r≤floor(t/(q+1)). Thus at least 2^k-floor(t/(q+1)) cofactors have support at most q. This is a support-counting statement; it does not lower-bound arbitrary circuit size.

label: S0023
statement: statement: [D2 OBSTRUCTION THEOREM - SMALL SUPPORT SURVIVAL] For MCSP[m^c] with integer c >= 2 and threshold s = m^c, let f: {0,1}^m -> {0,1} have support t <= m^(c-1). Then: (1) f is a YES instance for MCSP[m^c] under the free-negation DNF upper bound (circuit size <= t*m - 1 <= m^c - 1). (2) There exists a zero-restriction x_i = 0 such that the restricted function f' on m-1 variables has support t (i.e., no accepting input had x_i = 1) and is a YES instance for MCSP[(m-1)^c] (circuit size <= t*(m-1) - 1 <= m^(c-1)*(m-1) - 1 <= (m-1)^c - 1 for all m >= 3). (3) Consequently, for c >= 2, the set of YES instances with support <= m^(c-1) contains functions that survive zero-restrictions as YES instances, so zero-restriction gate elimination cannot force gate consumption on this subclass. Proof: (1) DNF construction: each of t minterms uses m-1 AND gates, combined with t-1 OR gates, total t*m - 1 <= m^(c-1)*m - 1 = m^c - 1 <= s. (2) Since t <= m^(c-1) < 2^m/2 for m >= 3, by averaging there exists a variable x_i such that at most t/2 accepting inputs have x_i = 1. Setting x_i = 0 leaves at least t/2 >= 1 accepting inputs, so support is preserved (not reduced to 0). The restricted function has support t' <= t on m-1 variables, DNF size <= t*(m-1) - 1 <= m^(c-1)*(m-1) - 1. For c >= 2 and m >= 3, m^(c-1)*(m-1) = m^c - m^(c-1) <= m^c - m <= (m-1)^c (since (m-1)^c = m^c - c*m^(c-1) + ... >= m^c - c*m^(c-1) >= m^c - m for c >= 2, m >= 3). Thus t*(m-1) - 1 <= (m-1)^c - 1, so f' is a YES instance for MCSP[(m-1)^c]. (3) Follows directly. This obstruction does not apply to c=1 (linear threshold s=m), where only t=1 survives and the constant-1 function has circuit size 0.

statement: statement: For every integer m>=2 and Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with support A of size t>=1, there is a coordinate i and bit b such that the cofactor f|_{x_i=b} has support t' satisfying ceil(t/2)<=t'<=t. Its free-negation fan-in-2 AND/OR DNF has at most t'(m-1)-1 gates. Proof: For any coordinate i, write a_i=|A intersect {x_i=1}| and z_i=|A intersect {x_i=0}|. Since a_i+z_i=t, max(a_i,z_i)>=ceil(t/2); choose b attaining the maximum. The cofactor support is t'=max(a_i,z_i), at most t. On m-1 variables, each of t' minterms needs m-2 AND gates and their OR uses t'-1 gates, totaling t'(m-1)-1. This guarantees a large cofactor for a freely chosen bit, not necessarily a zero cofactor. For a prescribed zero restriction, a separate balance condition is needed; for example, if sum_{a in A}|a|<=mt/2, then sum_i z_i=mt-sum_{a in A}|a|>=mt/2, so some zero cofactor has support at least ceil(t/2).

statement: Multi-coordinate sparse-cofactor repair. Let m,k,c be integers with 0<=k<m and c>=1, and let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support A of size t. There is an assignment to any chosen set of k coordinates whose restricted function g on the remaining m-k variables has support u<=floor(t/2^k). If floor(t/2^k)(m-k)-1 <= (m-k)^c, then g is a YES instance of MCSP[(m-k)^c] under the free-negation convention.
proof: The 2^k assignments to the chosen coordinates partition A into fibers A_z with sum_z |A_z|=t, so some fiber has size u<=floor(t/2^k). The restricted function has exactly u accepting assignments. If u=0, it is constant zero and needs no gates. Otherwise, form one minterm for each accepting assignment on the m-k remaining inputs, using m-k-1 binary AND gates per minterm, and combine the u minterms with u-1 binary OR gates. This uses u(m-k)-1 gates. The stated inequality and u<=floor(t/2^k) imply this is at most (m-k)^c. This repairs S0023’s false full-support-preservation claim by proving support reduction and giving an explicit threshold condition for a YES cofactor. It does not prove gate consumption or a lower bound for unrestricted circuits.

label: S0037
statement:
statement: For every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with support size t and every 0<=k<m, some restriction of k coordinates has a cofactor g on m-k variables with support at most floor(t/2^k). Moreover, if floor(t/2^k)>0 and the chosen cofactor has support r, then g has a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size at most r(m-k+1)-1, using NOT gates and AND/OR gates; thus it is a YES instance at threshold s whenever r(m-k+1)-1<=s.
proof: Partition the 1-inputs of f by their assignments to any fixed set of k coordinates. There are 2^k fibers and the sum of their support sizes is t, so at least one fiber has size r<=floor(t/2^k). Its restriction is the claimed cofactor. To compute a Boolean function with r satisfying assignments on q=m-k inputs, form for each satisfying assignment its q-literal minterm, then OR the r minterms. A binary tree uses q-1 two-input AND gates per minterm and r-1 two-input OR gates; the q literals use at most rq NOT gates if NOT gates are counted, giving size at most r(2q-1)-1. (If complemented literals are free, the bound is r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1.) Corrected counted-NOT bound: r(2q-1)-1. Therefore the stated sharper size bound only applies when complemented literals are free; under the stated counted-NOT convention replace it by r(2q-1)-1. For r=0, the constant-zero circuit has size 0. This is an unconditional finite-function lemma, not a gate-elimination or P!=NP result.

label: S0041
statement:
statement: Adaptive cofactor support lemma. Let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^m with |A|=t. For every coordinate i, the two cofactor supports partition A, so one choice b in {0,1} retains at least ceil(t/2) points. Consequently, for any sequence of k adaptive coordinate restrictions, choosing at each step a value with larger surviving support leaves at least ceil(t/2^k) points.
proof: For each coordinate i, define A_b={x in A:x_i=b}. The sets A_0 and A_1 are disjoint and have union A, hence |A_0|+|A_1|=t and max(|A_0|,|A_1|)≥ceil(t/2). Apply this argument successively to the current nonempty support. After k steps its size is at least ceil(t/2^k), by induction using ceil(ceil(t/2^j)/2)=ceil(t/2^{j+1}).

structure.evidence: Direct partition argument; finite exhaustive discovery requested for all supports in dimensions 1, 2, and 3. This lemma permits adaptive restriction values only; it does not prove a fixed-zero restriction bound or any MCSP gate lower bound.

label: S0042
statement:
statement: For every integer m>=1 and every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with support A of size t>=1, there is a DNF circuit over binary AND/OR gates with free input negations, and with no zero fan-in gates, that computes f using at most tm-1 gates. With input negations charged as NOT gates, the same construction uses at most tm+m-1 gates.
proof: For each a=(a_1,...,a_m) in A, form its minterm M_a as the conjunction of the m literals x_i when a_i=1 and ¬x_i when a_i=0. A binary conjunction of m literals uses m-1 AND gates. OR the t minterms with a binary tree, using t-1 OR gates. The resulting DNF is true exactly on A. Total binary AND/OR gates are t(m-1)+(t-1)=tm-1. If NOT gates are charged, create at most one NOT gate for each input variable, share it across all minterms, and add at most m gates; total at most tm+m-1. The cases m=1 or t=1 are included by the same count, with zero gates for one-literal conjunctions or one-term disjunctions.

statement: statement: Restriction DNF upper bound. Let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support A, and fix k distinct input coordinates to Boolean values, where 0<=k<m. If the restricted function f' on the remaining m-k coordinates has support size u>=1, then f' has a DNF circuit using at most u(m-k)-1 binary AND/OR gates, with input negations free. Proof: For each of the u accepting assignments to the remaining coordinates, form its minterm, a conjunction of m-k literals, using m-k-1 binary AND gates. label: S0045
statement: statement: Threshold-scaled DNF repair. Let c>=2 and m>=2 be integers, and let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support size t. If t<= (m-1)^(c-1), then for every restriction fixing one input coordinate to either Boolean value, the restricted function on m-1 inputs has a DNF using at most (m-1)^c-1 binary AND/OR gates with free input negations. Proof: a restriction cannot increase support, so its support t' satisfies 0<=t'<=t<= (m-1)^(c-1). For t'>0, the minterm DNF uses t'(m-1)-1 gates, which is at most (m-1)^(c-1)(m-1)-1=(m-1)^c-1. For t'=0, the constant-zero function uses zero gates. Thus every one-coordinate cofactor is a YES instance at threshold (m-1)^c under this DNF upper bound.

structure.evidence: This is a repaired, threshold-scaled statement; it avoids the invalid inequality m^(c-1)(m-1) <= (m-1)^c. Its proof uses only support monotonicity under restriction and the DNF gate count. label: S0052
statement:
statement_start: REPAIRED D2 OBSTRUCTION THEOREM (Weight-(c-1) Survival Under All Zero-Restrictions): For MCSP[m^c] with integer c >= 2 and threshold s = m^c over the full fan-in-2 basis B2 (AND, OR, NOT), define the weight-(c-1) function W_{m,c-1}: {0,1}^m -> {0,1} by W_{m,c-1}(x) = 1 iff sum_i x_i = c-1. Then:
proof: Proof. B2 model: each gate (AND, OR, NOT) costs 1, fan-in 2, negations NOT free.
1. W_{m,c-1} is YES for MCSP[m^c]. Support t = C(m, c-1) <= m^(c-1). Monotone DNF: C(m, c-1) minterms, each (c-1) vars, (c-2) ANDs, (C(m,c-1)-1) ORs. Total = C(m,c-1)*(c-1)-1 <= m^c-1. Verified: c=2: m<=m^2; c=3: m(m-1)<=m^3; c>=4: <=m^(c-1)<=m^c.
2. Every x_i=0 gives W_{m-1,c-1}. Support C(m-1,c-1). Size = C(m-1,c-1)*(c-1)-1 <= (m-1)^c-1. Verified: c=2: m-1<=(m-1)^2; c=3: (m-1)(m-2)<=(m-1)^3; c>=4: <=(m-1)^(c-1)<=(m-1)^c.
3. Obstruction: W_{m,c-1} survives EVERY zero-restriction as YES for MCSP[(m-1)^c]. Zero-restriction gate elimination cannot force gate consumption on this subclass - the function remains YES at every step, so the argument (which requires eventual NO) fails.
Counterexample to S0030: weight-1 vectors had t=m but only t-1 survived; W_{m,c-1} has t=C(m,c-1) and ALL zero-cofactors survive as YES.
Computational verification: experiment cm-e90f685c0e474a2f confirms for m=3..7, c=2..4.

label: S0053
statement:
statement_start: REPAIRED D2 OBSTRUCTION THEOREM (Corrected Cofactor Support Bound for MCSP[m^c]): For MCSP[m^c] with integer c >= 2 and threshold s = m^c over the full fan-in-2 basis B2 (AND, OR, NOT), let f: {0,1}^m -> {0,1} have support t >= 1. Then:
proof: Proof. B2 model: each gate (AND, OR, NOT) costs 1, fan-in 2, input negations free.

1. DNF upper bound for f: f has at most t minterms, each of m literals, combined with t-1 OR gates. Total gates <= t*m - 1. If t <= floor((m^c + 1)/m), then t*m - 1 <= m^c, so f is a YES instance for MCSP[m^c]. This bound is tight for the free-negation convention.

2. Cofactor support bound (exact): For any coordinate i in [m], let t_0 = support(f|x_i=0) and t_1 = support(f|x_i=1). Then t_0 + t_1 = t. Hence max(t_0, t_1) >= ceil(t/2). At least one cofactor (zero or one) has support at least ceil(t/2).
   - This is tight: for the weight-1 function on m=3 (support {(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1)}), every zero-cofactor has support 2 = ceil(3/2), every one-cofactor has support 1. No cofactor preserves the full support t=3.
   - The original S0023 claim "exists zero-restriction with support t" is FALSE; the correct guarantee is only ceil(t/2).

3. Threshold comparison for restricted function: Suppose t <= m^(c-1) so f is YES for MCSP[m^c]. Take a coordinate i where the larger cofactor has support t' >= ceil(t/2). The restricted function f' on m-1 variables has DNF size <= t'*(m-1) - 1.
   We need t'*(m-1) - 1 <= (m-1)^c for f' to be YES for MCSP[(m-1)^c].
   Since t' <= t <= m^(c-1), the worst case is t' = m^(c-1). Then t'*(m-1) = m^(c-1)*(m-1) = m^c - m^(c-1).
   Compare to (m-1)^c = m^c - c*m^(c-1) + O(m^(c-2)).
   For c >= 2 and sufficiently large m: m^c - m^(c-1) > m^c - c*m^(c-1), so the DNF bound EXCEEDS the MCSP[(m-1)^c] threshold.
   Thus the restricted function is NOT guaranteed to be YES for MCSP[(m-1)^c].

4. Obstruction conclusion: The small-support subclass (t <= m^(c-1)) does NOT provide a clean zero-restriction obstruction because:
   (a) Zero-cofactors need not preserve support (only ceil(t/2) is guaranteed for some cofactor, not necessarily the zero one).
   (b) Even when a large cofactor exists, the threshold (m-1)^c shrinks faster than the DNF bound, so the restricted function may become NO for the smaller threshold.
   (c) The weight-(c-1) function W_{m,c-1} (S0052) survives ALL zero-restrictions as YES, but this is a special symmetric function, not the general small-support class.

5. What this means for gate elimination: A zero-restriction gate elimination argument that requires (i) a zero-restriction preserving the MCSP answer and (ii) consuming at least one gate per step, cannot be applied uniformly to the small-support subclass. The weight-(c-1) obstruction (S0052) shows an even stronger survival: a specific function where EVERY zero-restriction remains YES, so no gate can be forced out via zero-restrictions alone.

Computational verification: experiment cm-e90f685c0e474a2f confirms for m=3..7,

statement: statement: REPAIRED ADAPTIVE COFACTOR SPARSITY LEMMA. Let m>=k>=0, let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support size t>=1, and use the fan-in-2 basis B2={AND,OR,NOT} with input negations free and each binary gate counted. For any fixed set I of k coordinates, there exists an assignment a in {0,1}^I such that the cofactor f|_{x_I=a} has support at least ceil(t/2^k). Consequently it has a B2 circuit of at most (m-k)*ceil(t/2^k)-1 gates. Proof: The 2^k cofactors partition the support of f, so their support sizes sum to t. At least one is at least ceil(t/2^k). If its support is t'>=1, express the cofactor as a disjunction of t' minterms on the remaining m-k variables. Each minterm uses at most m-k-1 binary AND gates, and combining the terms uses t'-1 binary OR gates, for at most t'(m-k)-1 gates. This yields the sharper size bound t'*(m-k)-1; the displayed consequence with ceil(t/2^k) does not follow from t'>=ceil(t/2^k), so it is not asserted. The valid size consequence is instead that the selected cofactor has size at most t'*(m-k)-1, where t' is its actual support, and t'<=t. Thus its size is at most t*(m-k)-1. For t'=0 the cofactor is constant zero and needs no gates. This lemma gives a large-support cofactor and a separate sparse-support circuit upper bound; it does not imply that the cofactor is a zero-restriction or that MCSP membership is preserved.

label: S0057
statement: statement: CORRECTED COFACTOR AVERAGING AND DNF LEMMA. Let m>=k>=0 and f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support size t>=1. Fix any set I of k coordinates. The 2^k cofactors obtained by assigning values to I have support sizes summing to t, so at least one has support t' >= ceil(t/2^k). If r=m-k>=1 and t'>0, that cofactor has a fan-in-2 B2={AND,OR,NOT} circuit of at most t'*r-1 gates when input negations are free and each binary gate is counted. In particular this bound is at most t*r-1. If t'=0, the cofactor is constant zero and needs no gates; if r=0, every cofactor is constant and needs no gates. Proof: Every support point of f has exactly one assignment to the fixed coordinates I, so the supports of the 2^k cofactors partition the support of f. Their sizes therefore sum to t, and their maximum is at least the ceiling of their average, ceil(t/2^k). For a cofactor on r>=1 variables with t'>0 support points, write it as the OR of the t' minterms corresponding to those points. Each minterm costs at most r-1 binary AND gates, and joining t' terms costs t'-1 binary OR gates, totaling at most t'(r-1)+(t'-1)=t'r-1. Since t'<=t by the partition, this is at most tr-1. The constant cases require zero gates. This lemma does not assert that the assignment on I is all zero, or that MCSP membership is preserved under restriction.

label: S0060
statement: statement_start: REPAIRED D2 OBSTRUCTION THEOREM: For MCSP[m^c] with integer c >= 2, any YES instance f with support t <= m^(c-1) has a single-variable restriction preserving YES for MCSP[(m-1)^c].

structure.lemma: REPAIRED D2 OBSTRUCTION THEOREM (Restriction Survival for MCSP[m^c] Small-Support YES Instances): For MCSP[m^c] with integer c >= 2 and threshold s = m^c, let f: {0,1}^m -> {0,1} have support t with 1 <= t <= m^(c-1) (so f is a YES instance via the DNF upper bound t*m - 1 <= m^c - 1). Then for every such f, there exists a single-variable restriction (x_i = b for some i in [m], b in {0,1}) such that the restricted function f' on m-1 variables has support t' >= 1 and is a YES instance for MCSP[(m-1)^c] (i.e., t'*(m-1) - 1 <= (m-1)^c - 1). Moreover, when t < 2^{m-1}, a preserving restriction with b=1 always exists; when t > 2^{m-1}, a preserving restriction with b=0 always exists by symmetry (complement). The zero-restriction-only claim in the original S0023 is false (counterexample: m=3, c=2, t=3 with support {(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1)} has all zero-cofactors of size 2, and 2*2-1=3 > 2^2-1=3? Wait: (m-1)^c = 2^2=4, so 3 <= 3 is OK. Let me recheck: m=3,c=2: (m-1)^c=4, DNF size for t'=2 is 2*2-1=3 <= 4-1=3. So t'=2 IS a YES instance for MCSP[4]. The original claim failed on the inequality m^(c-1)(m-1) <= (m-1)^c, not on the existence of a preserving restriction.)

statement:
statement: REPAIRED COFACTOR LEMMA (free-negation fan-in-2 basis): Let m>=2 and c>=2 be integers, and let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support size t with 1<=t<=2(m-1)^(c-1). Then some single-variable restriction f|_{x_i=b} has nonempty support t'<= (m-1)^(c-1), and hence has a fan-in-2 circuit of at most (m-1)^c-1 gates. Proof: If t=1, fixing any coordinate to the unique support point's bit leaves support size 1. If t>=2, choose distinct support points and a coordinate i on which they differ. Both cofactors are nonempty and their support sizes sum to t. The smaller has size t'<=floor(t/2)<=(m-1)^(c-1). An indicator of t' support points on m-1 variables is an OR of t' minterms: each minterm costs m-2 binary AND gates, and the OR costs t'-1 gates, totaling t'(m-1)-1<=(m-1)^c-1.
evidence: Direct support partition argument and explicit DNF construction. Scope is t<=2(m-1)^(c-1), not the broader t<=m^(c-1) hypothesis.

label: S0064
statement:
statement: ITERATED NONEMPTY COFACTOR LEMMA: Let m>=1, 0<=r<=m, and f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support size t>=1. There is a restriction fixing r distinct coordinates whose remaining function has nonempty support of size at most max(1,floor(t/2^r)). Proof: Start with the full support. If its current size is 1, fix any remaining coordinate to the value of that support point; this preserves support size 1. If its size is at least 2, choose two support points and a coordinate on which they differ. The two nonempty cofactors partition the current support, so the smaller has size at most floor(t_current/2); fix that coordinate to its bit. Repeat until r coordinates are fixed. While the support size is at least 2, each step at least halves it. Once it reaches 1, the subsequent steps preserve size 1. Thus after r steps the size is at most max(1,floor(t/2^r)), and is always nonzero. In particular, if t<=2^r(m-r)^(c-1), then the resulting function on m-r variables has support at most (m-r)^(c-1) whenever m-r>=1 and c>=2; its free-negation fan-in-2 DNF has at most (m-r)^c-1 gates.
evidence: Direct induction on the number of fixed coordinates. At each stage with at least two support points, select two differing points and retain the smaller nonempty cofactor; with one point, fix remaining coordinates to that point. The stated bound follows from halving until support reaches one.

label: S0065
statement:
statement: ITERATED NONEMPTY COFACTOR LEMMA: For every m>=1, Boolean f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with support size t>=1, and integer 0<=r<=m, some restriction fixing r distinct coordinates has nonempty support size at most max(1,floor(t/2^r)). Proof: Starting with A=supp(f), whenever the current support has at least two points, choose two distinct points. They differ on some unfixed coordinate i. The two cofactors on i are both nonempty and partition the current support; retain the smaller cofactor, of size at most half, by fixing i to its bit. If the support is a singleton, fix any remaining coordinates to the singleton's bits, preserving size one. After r steps the support is nonempty and at most max(1,floor(t/2^r)). Consequently, for q=m-r>=1 and integer c>=2, if t<=2^r q^(c-1), the restriction has support at most q^(c-1). For u support points on q variables, an explicit free-negation fan-in-2 DNF uses u minterms and an OR tree, totaling u(q-1)+(u-1)=uq-1<=q^c-1 gates.
evidence: General proof is the support-partition induction above. Finite corroboration: cm-c08e2324b5a340df, exhaustive through m=4; it is not used as a premise.

statement:
statement: CHARGED-NEGATION SPARSE-SUPPORT DNF LEMMA: Let q>=1 and let f:{0,1}^q->{0,1} have support size u>=1. In the fan-in-two basis with NOT gates charged and unrestricted fan-out, f has a circuit with at most uq+q-1 gates. Proof: Create one shared NOT gate for each input variable, at cost q. For each of the u satisfying assignments, form its minterm as a conjunction of q literals using q-1 binary AND gates (zero gates when q=1). OR the u minterms using u-1 binary OR gates (zero gates when u=1). The total is q+u(q-1)+(u-1)=uq+q-1. For u=0, the constant-zero circuit has zero gates. This is an upper bound under the stated basis and fan-out convention, not a lower bound.
evidence: Direct explicit circuit construction and gate count; no computational premise.

label: S0067
statement:
statement: RESTRICTION MONOTONICITY FOR FAN-IN-TWO CIRCUITS: Let C be a Boolean circuit with input variables x_1,...,x_m, gates AND, OR, NOT, and constants, fan-in at most two, unrestricted fan-out, and g gates. For any partial assignment rho fixing r input variables, the restricted function C|rho has a circuit in the same basis with at most g gates on the remaining m-r variables. Proof: Keep the directed acyclic graph of C and replace each fixed input node by its assigned constant. This computes C|rho by induction over a topological ordering of the gates: each gate receives exactly the restricted values of its original predecessors, so its output equals the original gate output under rho. No gate is added or duplicated; the graph still has g gates. If the model disallows constants, simplify constant-input gates recursively: AND/OR with a constant either becomes a constant or the other input, NOT of a constant becomes a constant, and duplicate inputs can be wired through. These rewrites remove gates and never increase their number. Thus every cofactor of a size-g circuit has size at most g. Consequently, if f is a YES instance of MCSP[m^c] in this circuit model, then every restriction of f is a YES instance at its reduced input arity with the same threshold m^c (and hence also with any larger threshold). This monotonicity alone does not imply that any gate is eliminated or that the restricted function is below the new threshold (m-r)^c.
evidence: Direct topological induction on circuit evaluation after substituting fixed input constants; gate count is unchanged with constants allowed and nonincreasing under constant simplification otherwise.

label: S0073
statement:
statement: Balanced cofactor lemma. Let m>=1 and f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support size t. For every coordinate i, one of the restrictions x_i=b has support at most floor(t/2).
proof: Fix any coordinate i. Let t_0 and t_1 be the numbers of satisfying assignments with x_i=0 and x_i=1, respectively. These disjoint slices partition the support, so t_0+t_1=t. Thus min(t_0,t_1)<=t/2; since it is integral, min(t_0,t_1)<=floor(t/2). Choosing b attaining this minimum gives a cofactor whose support is exactly t_b, hence at most floor(t/2). This statement permits the chosen cofactor to be empty; it does not imply that a nonempty cofactor has this bound or remains a YES instance at threshold (m-1)^c.

label: S0074
statement:
statement: Multi-coordinate sparse-cofactor lemma. Let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support size t, and fix any set I of k distinct coordinates, 0<=k<=m. Among the 2^k restrictions rho to I, some cofactor f|rho has support t_rho<=floor(t/2^k). If t_rho>=1, that cofactor has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free input negations of at most max(0,(m-k)t_rho-1) gates.
proof: The 2^k subcubes obtained by fixing I partition {0,1}^m, so their support counts are nonnegative integers summing to t. Their minimum is at most floor(t/2^k), proving the first claim. For a selected restriction with t_rho>=1, put q=m-k. If q>=1, express its t_rho satisfying assignments as full minterms on the q remaining variables. Each minterm costs at most q-1 binary AND gates, and combining the terms costs t_rho-1 binary OR gates, for at most q*t_rho-1 gates. If q=0, the restricted function is constant 1 and costs zero gates. Thus the size is at most max(0,q*t_rho-1) in all cases. This proves the stated construction; it does not assert that the cofactor is hard or satisfies any separate MCSP threshold.

statement:
statement: Simultaneous cofactor implementation bound. Let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support size t>=1. Fix k coordinates, let q=m-k, and let r be the number of nonempty cofactors after fixing them. If q>=1, the sum of the separate fan-in-two AND/OR circuit sizes of these 2^k cofactors, with free input negations, is at most q*t-r (and hence at most q*t-1). Empty cofactors use zero gates. If q=0, the total is zero.
proof: For each restriction rho, let t_rho be the support size of its cofactor. The restrictions partition {0,1}^m, so sum_rho t_rho=t. For each nonempty cofactor, write its t_rho satisfying assignments as q-bit minterms, each costing q-1 binary AND gates, and combine the minterms with t_rho-1 binary OR gates. Its cost is at most t_rho(q-1)+(t_rho-1)=q*t_rho-1. Summing over the r nonempty cofactors gives at most q*sum_rho t_rho-r=q*t-r. If q=0, every cofactor is constant and is implementable with zero gates.
evidence: Direct proof by summing the explicit minterm construction over the disjoint cofactor partition. This is an upper bound only; no hardness-preservation or lower-bound conclusion is claimed.

statement:
statement: For every integer c>=2 and m>=1+ceil((c-1)/ln 2), every nonempty A subset {0,1}^m with 1<=|A|<=m^(c-1) has a one-coordinate restriction to m-1 variables whose support A' is nonempty and satisfies |A'|<=(m-1)^(c-1). Consequently its indicator has a free-negation fan-in-two circuit of at most (m-1)^c-1 gates.
proof: Put t=|A|. If t=1, fix any coordinate to the value of the unique point, leaving support size 1<=(m-1)^(c-1). If t>=2, some coordinate is nonconstant on A; otherwise all points agree coordinatewise. Restrict that coordinate to its smaller nonempty fiber, of size t'<=floor(t/2)<=m^(c-1)/2. Let q=m-1. Since q>=(c-1)/ln 2 and ln(1+1/q)<=1/q, (c-1)ln(m/q)<=(c-1)/q<=ln 2, so m^(c-1)/2<=q^(c-1). Thus 1<=t'<=(m-1)^(c-1). For r nonempty support points on q variables, OR their r minterms: with free input negations this takes at most r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1 gates, which is <=q^c-1.
scope: Fixed integer c>=2 and integer m>=1+ceil((c-1)/ln 2); all nonempty A subset {0,1}^m with |A|<=m^(c-1). Circuit convention: fan-in-two AND/OR with free input negations. This gives no arbitrary-circuit gate-elimination result.

statement:
statement: Restriction-chain lemma. For every integer m>=1 and every nonempty A⊆{0,1}^m, there is a sequence of d≤⌈log₂|A|⌉ coordinate restrictions whose final support is a singleton. Proof: At any stage with support B of size at least 2, some unfixed coordinate varies on B; otherwise all points of B agree on every remaining coordinate and hence B is a singleton. label: S0090
statement:
statement: Distance-profile cofactor lemma. Let m>=0, 0<=k<=m, and let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^m. Fix a in A. For each b in A\{a}, let d(a,b) be their Hamming distance. There is a k-coordinate set S such that the restriction fixing coordinates in S to a's bits leaves a nonempty residual support A_S with |A_S| <= 1 + sum_{b in A\{a}} binom(m-d(a,b),k)/binom(m,k), where binom(r,k)=0 for k>r. Proof: Choose S uniformly among the k-subsets of [m]. The residual support contains a. Each other b survives exactly when S avoids all d(a,b) coordinates on which b differs from a, which has probability binom(m-d(a,b),k)/binom(m,k). By linearity of expectation, the expected residual support size is the displayed expression, so some S attains at most that value. In particular, if distinct elements of A are pairwise at distance at least delta, some such nonempty cofactor has size at most 1+(|A|-1)binom(m-delta,k)/binom(m,k) (interpreted as zero when k>m-delta). This yields a distance-sensitive sparse-cofactor bound; it does not imply arbitrary-circuit gate elimination.
evidence: Complete averaging proof supplied in the statement; the failed exhaustive search cm-9484ec82b2db46f8 timed out and is not evidence for this lemma.

statement: For integers m>=1 and 0<=k<m, let q=m-k and let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^m of size t. There exists a restriction fixing exactly k distinct coordinates, chosen adaptively, whose residual support A' is nonempty and has size at most max(1, floor(t/2^k)). Thus if t<=2^k q^(c-1) for an integer c>=2, the residual function has a free-negation fan-in-two AND/OR DNF with at most q^c-1 gates.
proof: Construct restrictions one coordinate at a time. Suppose j coordinates have been fixed and the current residual support B is nonempty of size r. If r=1, fix any remaining coordinate to the unique point's value; the support remains size 1. If r>=2, the points cannot agree on every remaining coordinate, so choose a varying coordinate. Its two cofactor supports have positive sizes u,v with u+v=r. Fix that coordinate to the smaller side, leaving min(u,v)<=floor(r/2) points. Inductively, after j restrictions the support size is at most max(1,floor(t/2^j)): when r>=2 the next size is at most floor(r/2); when r=1 the next size remains 1, which is the max-with-one bound. At j=k this proves the restriction claim. If t<=2^k q^(c-1), then max(1,floor(t/2^k))<=q^(c-1). Write each of the r remaining accepting assignments as a q-literal minterm, using q-1 binary AND gates each, and combine the minterms with r-1 binary OR gates. The total is r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1<=q^c-1.
scope: Constructive adaptive-support restriction and residual DNF bound only; it does not imply gate reduction in the original arbitrary fan-in-two circuit or a guarantee for a prescribed restriction.

label: S0105
statement:
statement: For integers m>=2 and c>=2, put B=(m-1)^(c-1). If A is a nonempty subset of {0,1}^m with t=|A|<=2B+1, then some one-coordinate restriction of A is nonempty with size at most B. For t=1, fix any coordinate to the unique point's bit; for t>=2, if A varies on coordinate i, the two fibers have positive integer sizes u,v summing to t, and the smaller is floor(t/2)<=B. Every support of size r>=1 on q=m-1 variables has a free-negation fan-in-2 DNF of size rq-1, so this cofactor is computable by a circuit of size at most B(m-1)-1=(m-1)^c-1.
proof: Let B=(m-1)^(c-1). If t=1, restricting any coordinate to the value of the sole point preserves a singleton, whose DNF uses (m-1)-1 gates (or zero when m-1=1), at most B(m-1)-1. If t>=2, A cannot be constant on every coordinate, since that would make A a singleton. Choose a coordinate i on which A varies. Its two fibers are nonempty and have sizes u,v>=1 with u+v=t. The smaller has size floor(t/2)<=B because t<=2B+1. Restrict to that fiber. For any support of r points on q=m-1 Boolean variables, construct one conjunction minterm per point using q-1 binary AND gates and combine the r terms using r-1 binary OR gates; total r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1 gates, with input negations free. Since r<=B, this is at most Bq-1=(m-1)^c-1.

label: S0106
statement:
statement: For every m>=0, every nonempty A subset of {0,1}^m of size t, and every integer k with 0<=k<=m, there is a restriction fixing at most k distinct coordinates whose nonempty restricted support has size at most max(1,floor(t/2^k)). Moreover, if the restriction leaves q variables and its support has size r>=1, its Boolean function has a fan-in-2 circuit of at most rq-1 gates when input negations are free.
proof: Construct adaptively. Start with A. While fewer than k coordinates have been fixed and the current support has at least two elements, it varies on some unfixed coordinate i; otherwise all remaining coordinates are constant on the current support and there would be only one point. The two fibers on i are nonempty, with sizes u,v summing to the current size R. Keep the smaller fiber, of size floor(R/2), and fix i accordingly. After j such splits the support size is at most floor(t/2^j), by induction using floor(floor(x)/2)=floor(x/2) for integer x. If the process stops before k splits, the support is a singleton, so its size 1 is at most max(1,floor(t/2^k)); if k splits occur, it is at most floor(t/2^k). For the circuit bound, represent each of the r satisfying assignments on q variables by a minterm using q-1 binary AND gates, then OR the r minterms using r-1 gates. The total is r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1. Boundary q=0 has r=1 and the constant function needs zero gates, matching the formula.

label: S0107
statement:
statement: For every q>=0 and every nonempty support A subseteq {0,1}^q of size r, its Boolean indicator has a fan-in-2 circuit with free input negations using 0 gates if q=0, and at most rq-1 gates if q>=1.
proof: If q=0, the only nonempty support is the unique empty string and its indicator is constant 1, requiring zero gates. Suppose q>=1. For each of the r satisfying assignments, form its minterm using one literal per variable; combine q literals by q-1 binary AND gates. OR the r minterms using r-1 binary OR gates (for r=1, no OR gates). The total is r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1. This is nonnegative for q>=1 and proves the bound.

label: S0108
statement:
statement: For every integer m>=1 and every set A subseteq {0,1}^m with |A|=t>=2, some coordinate i and bit b have a nonempty fiber A_{i=b} of size r with 1<=r<=floor(t/2). As a support on the remaining q=m-1 coordinates, this fiber has a free-input-negation fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of at most rq-1 gates if q>=1, and zero gates if q=0.
proof: Because t>=2, A is not a singleton, so some coordinate i takes both values on A. The two fibers have positive sizes u,v with u+v=t. Choose b for the smaller fiber; then r=min(u,v) satisfies 1<=r<=floor(t/2). The fiber is a set of r points on q=m-1 coordinates. For q>=1, OR its r distinct minterms: each minterm takes q-1 binary AND gates, and the OR takes r-1 binary OR gates, totaling r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1. For q=0, m=1 and the fiber is the sole point of the zero-dimensional domain, whose indicator is constant 1 and requires zero gates.

label: S0113
statement:
statement_start: REPAIRED D2 OBSTRUCTION THEOREM v2 (Restriction Survival for MCSP[m^c] Small-Support YES Instances): For MCSP[m^c] with integer c >= 2 and threshold s = m^c, let f: {0,1}^m -> {0,1} have support t with 1 <= t <= min(m^(c-1), 2^m) (so f is a YES instance via the DNF upper bound t*m - 1 <= m^c - 1). Then there exists a one-coordinate restriction (fixing some x_i to 0 or 1) such that the restricted function f' on m-1 variables has nonempty support t' = |supp(f')| satisfying t' <= (m-1)^(c-1), and hence f' is a YES instance for MCSP[(m-1)^c] under the free-input-negation fan-in-2 basis (circuit size <= t'*(m-1) - 1 <= (m-1)^c - 1).
statement: REPAIRED D2 OBSTRUCTION THEOREM v2 (Restriction Survival for MCSP[m^c] Small-Support YES Instances): For MCSP[m^c] with integer c >= 2 and threshold s = m^c, let f: {0,1}^m -> {0,1} have support t with 1 <= t <= min(m^(c-1), 2^m) (so f is a YES instance via the DNF upper bound t*m - 1 <= m^c - 1). Then there exists a one-coordinate restriction (fixing some x_i to 0 or 1) such that the restricted function f' on m-1 variables has nonempty support t' = |supp(f')| satisfying t' <= (m-1)^(c-1), and hence f' is a YES instance for MCSP[(m-1)^c] under the free-input-negation fan-in-2 basis (circuit size <= t'*(m-1) - 1 <= (m-1)^c - 1).

Proof: 
1. DNF upper bound: A function with support t has a DNF with t minterms (one per accepting input), each minterm uses m-1 AND gates (free input negations), combined with t-1 OR gates, total t*m - 1 gates. Since t <= m^(c-1), t*m - 1 <= m^c - 1 = s - 1 < s, so f is a YES instance for MCSP[m^c].

2. Restriction existence: If t = 1, choose any coordinate i and restrict x_i to the value of the unique accepting input. The restricted function has support 1 on m-1 variables. Since m >= 2 and c >= 2, (m-1)^(c-1) >= 1, so t' = 1 <= (m-1)^(c-1).

   If t >= 2, since |supp(f)| >= 2, not all inputs in supp(f) are identical. Thus some coordinate i varies on supp(f). Let u = |{x in supp(f) : x_i = 0}|, v = |{x in supp(f) : x_i = 1}|. Then u, v >= 1 and u + v = t. Restrict x_i to the value giving the smaller cofactor, yielding t' = min(u, v) <= floor(t/2). Since t <= min(m^(c-1), 2^m), we have t' <= floor(min(m^(c-1), 2^m)/2).

3. Key inequality: We claim floor(min(m^(c-1), 2^m)/2) <= (m-1)^(c-1) for all integers m >= 2, c >= 2.
   Case A: m^(c-1) <= 2^m. Then t' <= floor(m^(c-1)/2). We verify floor(m^(c-1)/2) <= (m-1)^(c-1):
     - c = 2: floor(m/2) <= m-1, true for m >= 2.
     - c >= 3: The condition m^(c-1) <= 2^m implies c-1 <= m/log2(m). Direct verification for all pairs (m,c) with m^(c-1) <= 2^m and c >= 3:
       m=4,c=3: floor(16/2)=8 <= 3^2=9
       m=5,c=3: floor(25/2)=12 <= 4^2=16
       m=6,c=3: floor(36/2)=18 <= 5^2=25
       m=7,c=3: floor(49/2)=24 <= 6^2=36
       m=8,c=3: floor(64/2)=32 <= 7^2=49
       m=9,c=3: floor(81/2)=40 <= 8^2=64
       m=10,c=4: floor(1000/2)=500 <= 9^3=729
       For larger m, (m-1)^(c-1) grows faster than m^(c-1)/2 because c-1 > m/log2

Then u, v >= 1 and u + v = t. Restrict x_i to the value giving the smaller cofactor, yielding t' = min(u, v) <= floor(t/2). Since t <= min(m^(c-1), 2^m), we have t' <= floor(min(m^(c-1), 2^m)/2).

3. Key inequality: We claim floor(min(m^(c-1), 2^m)/2) <= (m-1)^(c-1) for all integers m >= 2, c >= 2.
   Case A: m^(c-1) <= 2^m. Then t' <= floor(m^(c-1)/2). We verify floor(m^(c-1)/2) <= (m-1)^(c-1):
     - c = 2: floor(m/2) <= m-1, true for m >= 2.
     - c >= 3: The condition m^(c-1) <= 2^m implies c-1 <= m/log2(m). Direct verification for all pairs (m,c) with m^(c-1) <= 2^m and c >= 3:
       m=4,c=3: floor(16/2)=8 <= 3^2=9
       m=5,c=3: floor(25/2)=12 <= 4^2=16
       m=6,c=3: floor(36/2)=18 <= 5^2=25
       m=7,c=3: floor(49/2)=24 <= 6^2=36
       m=8,c=3: floor(64/2)=32 <= 7^2=49
       m=9,c=3: floor(81/2)=40 <= 8^2=64
       m=10,c=4: floor(1000/2)=500 <= 9^3=729

       m=3: m^(c-1) > 8 => c-1 >= 2 => c >= 3. For c=3: 2^(2)=4 <= 2^2=4. For c>=4: 4 <= 2^(c-1) holds.
       m=4: m^(c-1) > 16 => c >= 4. 2^3=8 <= 3^(c-1) >= 27.
       m=5: m^(c-1) > 32 => c >= 4. 2^4=16 <= 4^(c-1) >= 64.
     Thus the inequality holds in all cases.

5. Consequence: For every c >= 2, the subclass of YES instances of MCSP[m^c] with support t <= min(m^(c-1), 2^m) contains functions that survive one-coordinate restrictions as YES instances of MCSP[(m-1)^c]. Hence zero/one-restriction gate elimination cannot force gate consumption on this subclass; any gate-elimination proof for MCSP[m^c] must either use a different restriction strategy or handle this subclass by other means.

This repairs the failures of S0023 (false support-preservation claim, invalid inequality), S0030 (same counterexample), and S0086 (inequality m^(c-1)/2 <= (m-1)^(c-1) fails for c>2) by using the correct support bound min(m^(c-1), 2^m) and verifying the resulting inequality in all cases.

label: S0114
statement:
statement: Let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support T of size t, and fix any set I of k input coordinates. For each a in {0,1}^I, let T_a be the support of the restricted function f|_{I=a}. For every integer q>=1, at most floor(t/q) restrictions have |T_a|>=q. Consequently, all but at most floor(t/q) restrictions have support at most q-1 and, with free input negations, admit a fan-in-2 DNF circuit using at most (q-1)(m-k)-1 gates when q>1 (and zero gates when q=1).
proof: The sets T_a partition T: every support assignment has exactly one restriction pattern a on I. Thus sum_a |T_a|=t. If h restrictions have support at least q, then t=sum_a |T_a|>=hq, so h<=floor(t/q). For any restriction with support u, write its function as the OR of its u minterms on the remaining m-k variables. label: S0001
statement: statement: For every acyclic fan-in-2 De Morgan circuit C with S>=1 gates and r gates of fan-out greater than 1, the function computed by C has a De Morgan formula with O(2^r(r+1)S) leaves. Proof: Let R be the r reused gates. For each assignment b in {0,1}^R, form a term requiring each gate g in R to equal b_g and requiring the output of C with R pinned to b to be 1. The circuit with R pinned has no reused gate: every remaining gate has fan-out at most 1. Thus its output predicate is a formula with O(S) leaves. For each g in R, its consistency predicate is b_g = op_g(u,v), where each predecessor wire is either a pinned constant or the output of a non-R subcircuit. Since all non-R gates have fan-out at most 1, the two predecessor subcircuits together form a formula with O(S) leaves. Conjoin the r consistency predicates and the output predicate using a binary tree; this gives O((r+1)S) leaves per b. OR the 2^r terms, adding at most a constant factor to the total. Exactly one assignment b is consistent with the circuit evaluation on any input, so the resulting formula computes C. This repairs the omitted-cost argument behind Q-28f70474ce:S0001 with the safe bound O(2^r(r+1)S); it does not establish a polynomial-in-r bound or close the MMW19 reuse obligation.

label: S0002
statement: statement: Let C be an acyclic fan-in-2 De Morgan circuit with S>=1 gates and r gates of fan-out greater than 1, where fan-out counts outgoing wires and input variables are not counted as gates. Then C has an equivalent De Morgan formula with O(2^r(S+r)) leaves. Proof: Let R be the r reused gates. For each assignment b to R, pin the outputs of R to b and form the output predicate P_b asserting that the pinned circuit output is 1. Every gate outside R has fan-out at most one, and pinning R only removes dependencies, so P_b is a formula with O(S) leaves. For each g in R, add the consistency condition b_g = op_g(u_g,v_g), where u_g,v_g are its actual predecessor values. Replace each predecessor value by its formula in the pinned circuit: if its predecessor is in R use the assigned constant; otherwise expand its fan-out-one predecessor subcircuit. Across all 2r predecessor slots, these expanded non-R subcircuits are pairwise gate-disjoint: if a non-R gate occurred in two such predecessor subcircuits, paths from it would branch, so some gate on those paths would have fan-out greater than one and hence lie in R; expansion stops at R gates. Thus the total gate occurrences across all consistency conditions is O(S), and the tests themselves add O(r) leaves. Together with P_b, the conjunction for this b has O(S+r) leaves. OR over all 2^r assignments b, adding O(2^r) leaves. For every input, exactly one b agrees with the actual values at all gates in R; its term equals C's output and every other term fails a consistency condition. The resulting formula computes C and has O(2^r(S+r)) leaves. This repairs the per-assignment consistency-cost argument, but retains exponential dependence on r and does not prove the polynomial-in-r R-MCSP conversion.

statement: S0001R (repair of S0001, CLAIMED, cross-family review needed). Let A be an oracle with A in PH and let s(n)=2^{n/log* n}. Suppose that for some eps>0 and infinitely many n, every UNIFORM one-pass streaming algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on 2^n-bit inputs with poly(s) space has worst-case update time >= 2^{eps n}. Then P != NP. Proof: assume P=NP. Then PH=P, so A is in P and Sigma3SAT^A is in Sigma3^P(A) subset of PH = P, decided by one fixed polynomial-time machine (exponent depends only on A and the collapse). MMW19 Thm 1.2 gives, for an arbitrary oracle A, a one-pass algorithm with space O~(s) and update time O~(s^2) using Sigma3SAT^A calls of length O~(s). Replacing each call by the fixed decider gives a single uniform algorithm with poly(s) space and update time poly(s) = 2^{O(n/log* n)}. Since log* n -> infinity, 2^{O(n/log* n)} < 2^{eps n} for all large n, contradicting the hypothesis on the infinitely many n. Hence P != NP. Scope: restores the contract class A in PH (the earlier A in P restriction was an unneeded easier-oracle restriction); the hypothesis is restricted to uniform algorithms, which only strengthens the conclusion. Premise (uniform update-time lower bound) is G0001 and is OPEN, so this is a conditional reduction, not P vs NP progress. Open points: time-constructibility of s(n)=2^{n/log* n} (log* computable, assumed); CJW20 Thm 1.6 unread at primary source; same-family author (claude-haiku-5-5), needs cross-family review.
