structure.lemma: NECESSARY CONDITION FOR THE RESIDUAL-DP SAVING (lane D). Setting as in S0007: prefix S (|S| = s), bottom block B (|B| = q), gate j with W_j = (W_jS, W_jB), t_j, lo_j = sum_{i in B} min(0, W_ji), hi_j = sum_{i in B} max(0, W_ji), L_j = sum_{i in S} min(0, W_ji), U_j = sum_{i in S} max(0, W_ji). Define the always-live set C = {j : lo_j < t_j - W_jS.x_S <= hi_j for every x_S in {0,1}^s}. Then (a) j in C iff t_j - U_j > lo_j and t_j - L_j <= hi_j; (b) C is contained in N(x_S) for every prefix x_S, so |N(x_S)| >= |C|. Consequently the residual-DP corollary (|N(x_S)| <= kappa q / log2(2aq+1) for all prefixes) forces |C| <= kappa q / log2(2aq+1). PROOF: (a) W_jS.x_S ranges over [L_j, U_j] and both endpoints are attained (x_S = indicator of the negative, resp. positive, weights), so the residual t_j - W_jS.x_S ranges exactly over [t_j - U_j, t_j - L_j]; it lies in (lo_j, hi_j] for all x_S iff t_j - U_j > lo_j and t_j - L_j <= hi_j. (b) If j in C, every residual lies in (lo_j, hi_j], so gate j is not clipped for any prefix and belongs to N(x_S) by definition. The consequence is immediate from (b). So the residual-DP procedure can save only on families where almost all gates are clipped for most prefixes; a family where a constant fraction of gates is in C is outside its saving regime, whatever the prefix split.

label: S0046
statement:
statement: PREFIX-RANK STATE BOUND. Let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_ji| <= M, t in Z^m, v in Z^m, T in Z. For x in {0,1}^n define the threshold circuit f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. For each prefix length k = 0..n, let S_k = {W_{1..k} . a : a in {0,1}^k} be the set of distinct partial sums of the first k columns. Let r_k = rank_Q(W_{1..k}) be the rational rank of the first k columns. Then |S_k| <= min(2^k, (2Mk+1)^{r_k}). Moreover, #SAT(f) can be computed by a dynamic program that maintains the exact counts for each element of S_k, and the total number of DP states over all k is sum_k |S_k| <= sum_k min(2^k, (2Mk+1)^{r_k}).
proof: For any a in {0,1}^k, W_{1..k}.a is an integer vector in Z^m with each coordinate bounded by Mk in absolute value (since |W_ji| <= M and a_j in {0,1}). Hence W_{1..k}.a lies in the box [-Mk, Mk]^m, which contains (2Mk+1)^m points. However, the image of {0,1}^k under the linear map W_{1..k} is contained in the Q-linear span of the columns of W_{1..k}, which has dimension r_k. The intersection of a box of side 2Mk+1 with an r_k-dimensional linear subspace over Q has at most (2Mk+1)^{r_k} integer points (a basis of the subspace gives an injective linear map to Q^{r_k}, and integer points map to integer points whose coordinates are bounded by the same box after a change of basis with determinant 1). Therefore |S_k| <= min(2^k, (2Mk+1)^{r_k}). The DP processes columns 1..n sequentially; at step k it stores the exact count of assignments a in {0,1}^k for each s in S_k. The transition from k to k+1 is s' = s + b * W_{*,k+1} for b in {0,1}. The final count for f(x)=1 is obtained by evaluating the threshold conditions on the full sum s in S_n and summing the corresponding counts. Correctness follows by induction on k.

statement: PREFIX-RANK STATE BOUND (repair of S0046). Let W be an integer m x n matrix with |W_ji| <= M, let W_k be its first k columns, r_k = rank_Q(W_k) >= 1, and S_k = {W_k a : a in {0,1}^k}. Then |S_k| <= min(2^k, (2Mk+1)^{r_k}).
proof: Pick r = r_k rows of W_k that are linearly independent; call the r x k matrix R. The rows of W_k lie in the row space of R, so W_k = G R for some rational m x r matrix G. Hence W_k a = G (R a), so |S_k| <= |{R a : a in {0,1}^k}|. Each entry of R a is an integer of absolute value at most Mk, so R a lies in a set of (2Mk+1)^r integer vectors. The bound 2^k is trivial. The determinant-1 basis-change argument of S0046 is withdrawn.

label: S0052
statement: LEMMA (touched-column bound). Let W, L, E be integer m x p matrices with W = L + E, max|L_ij| <= M, rank_Q(L) <= r, and E_ij = 0 outside a column set C with |C| = c. Then #{Wx : x in {0,1}^p} <= min(2^p, (2Mp+1)^r * 2^c). PROOF: (1) Let rows I (|I| = rank L <= r) be a Q-basis of the row space of L, and R = L_I. Each row of L is a Q-combination of rows of R, so Lx = Lambda(Rx) for a fixed rational matrix Lambda. (2) Rx is an integer vector with entries bounded by Mp in absolute value, so #{Rx} <= (2Mp+1)^r. (3) Ex = E_{.,C} x_C depends only on x_C, so #{Ex} <= 2^c. (4) Wx = Lambda(Rx) + Ex is a function of the pair (Rx, x_C), so #{Wx} <= #{(Rx, x_C)} <= (2Mp+1)^r 2^c. The trivial bound 2^p is also an upper bound. QED. Consequence: the thresholded prefix states [W_j x >= t_j] are functions of Wx, so the same bound holds for state counts. Asymptotically, with r = o(p / log p), M constant and c <= (1-delta) p, the state count is at most 2^{(1-delta+o(1)) p}. Correction of earlier record S-b2c28a4a0d: its claim that the saving disappears once k is a constant fraction of n is not established; this lemma bounds it only through c.

label: S0054
statement: LEMMA (M-free rank bound on bottom patterns). Let W in Q^{m x n} have rank r, t in Q^m, and P(W,t) = {(1[W_j.x >= t_j])_{j<=m} : x in {0,1}^n}. Then |P(W,t)| <= min(2^n, sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i)). PROOF. Factor W = U V with U in Q^{m x r}, V in Q^{r x n} (rank r). Put z = Vx. Then W_j.x = U_j.z, so the pattern is a function of z in the finite set Z = {Vx : x in {0,1}^n} subset of Q^r. Let D = {U_j.z - t_j : j, z in Z} and delta = min{|d| : d in D, d != 0} > 0 (finite set of rationals; if D = {0} there is no sign change to track). Choose eps in Q with 0 < eps < delta and t_j - eps not equal to U_j.z for all j and z in Z (finitely many exclusions). For z in Z: 1[U_j.z >= t_j] = 1[U_j.z > t_j - eps], because U_j.z >= t_j implies U_j.z > t_j - eps, and U_j.z < t_j implies U_j.z <= t_j - delta < t_j - eps. The hyperplanes H_j = {z : U_j.z = t_j - eps} avoid Z, so each z in Z lies in an open cell of the arrangement {H_j} in R^r, and the pattern is determined by that cell. Distinct patterns come from distinct cells. Rows U_j = 0 give constant sign and define no hyperplane; dropping them leaves m' <= m hyperplanes. A central fact (Buck 1943; Zaslavsky 1975): an arrangement of m' affine hyperplanes in R^r has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m',i) <= sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) cells. Hence |P| <= sum_{i<=r} C(m,i). Also |P| <= 2^n trivially. QED. Then W_j.x = U_j.z, so the pattern is a function of z in the finite set Z = {Vx : x in {0,1}^n} subset of Q^r. Let D = {U_j.z - t_j : j, z in Z} and delta = min{|d| : d in D, d != 0} > 0 (finite set of rationals; if D = {0} there is no sign change to track). Choose eps in Q with 0 < eps < delta and t_j - eps not equal to U_j.z for all j and z in Z (finitely many exclusions). For z in Z: 1[U_j.z >= t_j] = 1[U_j.z > t_j - eps], because U_j.z >= t_j implies U_j.z > t_j - eps, and U_j.z < t_j implies U_j.z <= t_j - delta < t_j - eps. For a prefix length p let L+_q(p) = sum_{i>p} max(0,E_qi), L-_q(p) = sum_{i>p} min(0,E_qi), and clip z_q to c_q(z,p) = clamp(z_q, t_q - L+_q(p) - 1, t_q - L-_q(p)). Then (a) #SAT f is computed exactly by the DP over keys (y_p, c(z_p,p)), where y_p = A x_{<=p} and z_p = E x_{<=p}; (b) the number of keys at step p is at most min{ 2^p, prod_k(||A_k^{<=p}||_1+1) * prod_q(L+_q(p)-L-_q(p)+2) }. statement: LEMMA W (window + state bound, repairs CLAIM 1). Setting as in the record: W = [C A ; E] with A in Z^{r x n}, |A|,|W| <= B, E in Z^{k x n}, thresholds t_j, weights v_j >= 1, V = sum_j v_j, prefix length p, suffix sums L-_j(p) = sum_{i>p} min(W_ji,0), L+_j(p) = sum_{i>p} max(W_ji,0). PROOF. (1) Decision rule: after reading x_1..x_p with partial sum s_j, gate j is decided true if s_j + L-_j(p) >= t_j, decided false if s_j + L+_j(p) < t_j, and undecided otherwise. Future sums lie in [s_j+L-_j, s_j+L+_j], so a decided gate keeps its value for every suffix; the DP is exact (dropping decided gates loses no information). (2) Window: a gate undecided at p has s_j in [t_j - L+_j(p), t_j - L-_j(p)), an interval of length L+_j - L-_j = sum_{i>p}|W_ji| <= (n-p)B, so it has at most (n-p)B+2 integer values. Thus the clamp of the record is not needed: undecided values are already windowed. (3) Normal rows: for j in N, s_j = U_j . y with y = A x_{<=p} in Z^r, |y_i| <= pB, so the undecided normal values are a function of y: at most (2pB+1)^r possibilities. It does not close G0001(i), G0001(iii), G0003 or G0006; it shrinks the constant of CLAIM 1 from (nB+3)^k to ((n-p)B+2)^k and corrects the claim that unclipped values are unbounded. statement: Proof. For j in [m] and x in {0,1}^p: W_{j,<=p} . x = sum_{i<=p} (sum_k U_{jk} A_{ki}) x_i + sum_{i<=p} E_{ji} x_i = sum_k U_{jk} y_k + sum_{i in T cap [p]} E_{ji} x_i, where y = A_{<=p} x_{<=p} in Z^r. So the whole state vector is a function of the pair (y, x restricted to T cap [p]). Since |y_k| <= B p, y takes at most (2Bp+1)^r values; the restriction takes at most 2^{|T cap [p]|} values. Counting pairs gives the bound; the bound 2^p is trivial. Since p <= n, (2Bp+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^r, and 2^s (2Bn+1)^r = 2^{s + r log2(2Bn+1)} <= 2^{(1-eps) n} under the stated condition. Sanity check: with s = 0 (pure rank r) it recovers the rank-r state bound. Scope: exact, for any m; T is one fixed set for the whole matrix, not per row. Not covered: per-row k-sparse E whose supports together cover all columns (the union support is then all n columns, so s = n).

Claim: the number of distinct prefix states over x in {0,1}^p is at most min(2^p, (2Bp+1)^r * 2^{|T cap [p]|}). Consequently, if s + r*log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-eps) n, every prefix state count is at most 2^{(1-eps) n}.

statement: CLAIMED (R0953). ROW-OUTLIER RANK LEMMA (row-sparse case of G0001(i)). Setting: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B_W; t in Z^m; T in Z; a set K of exceptional rows with |K| = k; every j outside K has W_j = U_j A with U_j in Z^r and A in Z^{r x n}, |A_ic| <= B_A (rows of A fixed, the same for all normal rows). Statement: N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} can be computed exactly by a DP whose number of states after reading x_1..x_p is at most (k+1)(2pB_A+1)^r ((n-p)B_W+1)^k. Hence N is computed in time poly(n,m) (k+1) (2nB_A+1)^r (nB_W+1)^k. In particular N is computed in time 2^{(1-eps)n} poly(n,m) whenever r log2(2nB_A+1) + k log2(nB_W+1) + log2(k+1) <= (1-eps) n. PROOF. Key after prefix p: (cnt, y = A x_{<=p}, sorted tuple of (q, s_q) for q in K undecided at p, with exact partial sums s_q = W_{q,<=p}.x_{<=p}). cnt in {0..k} counts exceptional rows already decided TRUE. A row q is decided at p when its future range [minfut, maxfut] lets it be fixed; decided-FALSE rows contribute nothing. Transition: reading x_{p+1} adds A_{.,p+1} to y and W_{q,p+1} to each undecided s_q, then decides rows. Exactness: the future count depends only on the key, because (i) decided exceptional rows are absorbed into cnt; (ii) for an undecided q the future outcome depends only on s_q; (iii) a normal row j satisfies W_j.x = U_j.(A x), so at the end it is decided by U_j.y_n >= t_j with y_n = y_p + A x_{>p}, which depends only on the key and the future bits. Counting: y lies in [-pB_A, pB_A]^r, so (2pB_A+1)^r values; for each q in K the entry is absent or s_q lies in the integer window [t_q - maxfut_q(p), t_q - minfut_q(p) - 1] of size maxfut - minfut <= (n-p)B_W, so at most (n-p)B_W+1 options; cnt gives k+1. Multiplying gives the bound. The DP is exact by (i)-(iii). SCOPE AND LIMITS: (a) needs k log2(nB_W+1) + r log2(2nB_A+1) <= (1-eps)n, so it covers rank r on all but k = o(n/log n) rows, not full-rank W (k=0, r=n fails). (b) Entry-spread error across all columns is NOT covered (G0012, G0013 remain open). (c) Whether hard m = n^alpha THR o THR families have all but o(n/log n) gates in an o(n/log n)-dim row span is open (G0002, G0006). (d) Numerical support: cm-8dc4437721694664 (360 exact cases, 0 mismatches). Reviewer: this may be judged a combination of known DP and rank techniques; confirms_closure is not assumed. Obligation closed: G0001 row-sparse subcase only.

statement: PREFIX-RANK STATE LEMMA (general, no factorisation). Let W be an m x n integer matrix with all entries in [-L, L], L >= 1. For 1 <= p <= n let rho_p = rank over Q of the prefix block W[:, 1..p]. Then the number of distinct prefix states {W[:,1..p] x : x in {0,1}^p} is at most min(2^p, (2Lp+1)^{rho_p}). PROOF: choose rho_p linearly independent rows R (a rho_p x p integer matrix) of the prefix block. Every other row of the prefix block is a rational combination of R, row_j = sum_i lambda_{ji} R_i, with lambda fixed by W and independent of x. So W_j,<=p x = sum_i lambda_{ji} (R_i x), and the whole state is a function of R x in Z^{rho_p}. Each entry of R x lies in [-Lp, Lp], a set of 2Lp+1 integers, so at most (2Lp+1)^{rho_p} values. The bound 2^p is trivial. Consequence: if rho_p * log2(2Ln+1) <= (1-eps) n for every prefix that is used, the state count is at most 2^{(1-eps) n}. SCOPE: this is S0081 with the hypothesis A,U,E replaced by 'the prefix rank is small'; for W of total rank r it gives rho_p <= r. It does NOT help full-rank W (rho_p = p gives only the trivial bound), and it does not handle near-low-rank W = UA+E unless the rank of W itself is small.

label: S0097
statement: LEMMA D1 (exact linear prefix-state limit). Claim (a): A x = A y iff A t = 0 with t = x - y in {-1,0,1}^p. Every nonzero t in {-1,0,1}^p arises as x - y with x = max(t,0) and y = max(-t,0), both in {0,1}^p, and x != y. So x -> Ax is injective on {0,1}^p iff no nonzero such t lies in ker A. If rank A = p then ker A = 0, so N(A) = 2^p. Claim (b), lower bound: pick r columns S with A_S of rank r. A_S is injective on Q^r, so the 2^r vectors A x with x in {0,1}^S (zero outside S) are distinct. Claim (b), upper bound: pick r linearly independent rows R of A. Every row of A is a rational combination of R, so A = M R with M rational, hence Ax = M(Rx). Each entry of Rx lies in [-Bp, Bp], so N(A) <= #{Rx} <= (2Bp+1)^r. The 2^p bound is trivial. Consequence: any DP whose state is the linear prefix vector Ax has at least 2^{rank A} states, and full-rank prefix blocks give exactly 2^p states. The rank DP saves only when r log2(2Bp+1) < p. This identifies the exact limit of the linear-state method and corrects the earlier open reading of G0003: for linear states the full-rank case is settled negatively, so any saving must come from non-linear state (thresholds or clipping) or from a different decomposition.

label: S0105
statement: L-PROD: CLAIMED. Proof. (1) Rows of R form a Q-basis of the row space, so each row k satisfies A_k = sum_{i in R} c_{k,i} A_i with rational c_{k,i}. Hence (Ax)_k = sum_i c_{k,i} (A_R x)_i, so Ax is a function of A_R x. (2) Thus N(A) <= |{A_R x : x in {0,1}^p}|. (3) For each i in R, (A_i x) is an integer in [sum_j min(a_ij,0), sum_j max(a_ij,0)], an interval of length ||A_i||_1, so it takes at most 1 + ||A_i||_1 values. (4) The image A_R x lies in the product of these intervals, which gives the product bound. (5) ||A_i||_1 <= Bp gives (1+Bp)^r; 2^{(1-eps)p} follows from r log2(1+Bp) <= (1-eps) p. Exact check of the product bound: cm-aff77c8e13b14bc5 (248 instances, 0 failures, 136 tight).

label: S0107
statement: CLAIMED. Proof of the rank bound: let E_R be E restricted to rows in R and E_C = E - E_R. The nonzero entries of E_C lie in columns of C, so rank(E_C) <= |C|. E_R has at most |R| nonzero rows, so rank(E_R) <= |R|. By subadditivity, rank(W) <= rank(P) + rank(E_R) + rank(E_C) <= r + |R| + |C|. The #SAT consequence uses the rank-r DP with a basis of rank(W) independent rows: the vector of clipped partial sums of the basis rows determines every other row's partial sum, because each row is a rational combination of the basis rows, so the DP is determinate and has at most (2Bn+1)^{rank W} states.

structure.lemma: Cover-rank lemma. Let W in Z^{m x n} with W = P + E, rank(P) <= r, and suppose every nonzero entry of E lies in a row indexed by R or a column indexed by C. Then rank(W) <= r + |R| + |C|. Consequence: exact #SAT of THR o THR with bottom matrix W is computed in time poly(m,n) (2Bn+1)^{rank W}, where B bounds |entries| of W, by the rank-r DP lemma applied with r := rank W. Saving 2^{(1-eps) n} iff r + |R| + |C| <= (1-eps) n / log2(2Bn+1).

label: S0110
statement: COROLLARY of S0108 (entrywise sparse error). Let W = UA + E in Z^{m x n} with |W_jl| <= B, rank_Q(UA) <= r, and let E have k nonzero entries supported on a column set S with |S| = s <= k. Then N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly with at most 2^s (2Bn+1)^r reachable states per column step. PROOF. W agrees with UA outside the columns S, so the submatrix of W on the columns outside S has rank at most r. Apply S0108 with S as the free columns (after a column permutation). No correction term is needed, because S0108 is exact. SAVING: holds when k + r log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-eps) n. SCOPE: nnz(E) = O(n) with rank r = O(n / log(Bn)). Sparse E with superlinear nnz is not covered. This is bookkeeping on S0108, not new progress toward G0002 in full. Not reviewed; CLAIMED and open until another session reviews it.

statement: L1 as stated in the lemma field: a correct bound on distinct output vectors of THR layers of a rank-r linear form system, with exact proof as recorded in the lemma field. Scope: any W of rank r, any real thresholds t; it bounds output vectors, not DP states and not a #SAT running time.

structure.gap: Does NOT close G0001(iii), G0003 or G0075. A saving for #SAT needs, in addition, a procedure that counts x in {0,1}^n per cell with cost below 2^{(1-eps)n}. Correction to G0075: the threshold for m = n is r <= (1/2 - eps) n (since sum_{i<=cn} C(n,i) <= 2^{n H(c)}, H(c) < 1 for c < 1/2), replacing the weaker (em/r)^r threshold r <= 0.32 n. For m = 2n the threshold is r <= 0.22 n.
structure.lemma: L1 (weight-free sign-pattern count, rank r). Let W in Q^{m x n} have rank r >= 1, t in Q^m, sigma(x) = (1[W_j . x >= t_j])_{j<=m}. Then |{sigma(x) : x in {0,1}^n}| <= min(2^n, sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i)). Proof: factor W = UA (U in Q^{m x r}, A in Q^{r x n}); Y = {Ax : x in {0,1}^n} is finite; delta = min |U_j . y - t_j| over y in Y with U_j . y != t_j (delta = 1 if none); s_j = t_j - delta/2. For y in Y, U_j . y >= t_j implies U_j . y > s_j, and U_j . y < t_j implies U_j . y <= t_j - delta < s_j, so sigma(x)_j = 1[U_j . y(x) > s_j] and no Y-point lies on any hyperplane {U_j . y = s_j}. Hence sigma(x) is the sign vector of a cell of the arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r; distinct cells have distinct sign vectors; the arrangement has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) cells (Buck 1943 / Zaslavsky). Zero rows U_j = 0 give constant signs and do not increase the count.

label: S0112
statement: LEMMA P1 (candidate, unreviewed). Let W in Z^{m x n}, t in Z^m, r = rank_Q(W). Then |{(1[W_j.x >= t_j])_{j<=m} : x in {0,1}^n}| <= sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i). Proof sketch: (a) integrality: W_j.x - t_j is an integer, so W_j.x >= t_j iff W_j.x > t'_j with t'_j = t_j - 1/2, and no cube point lies on a hyperplane {W_j.x = t'_j}. (b) Factor W = U L with L in Q^{r x n} of full row rank. Then W_j.x - t'_j = U_j.(Lx) - t'_j, so the pattern is a function of y = Lx in R^r off the affine hyperplanes {U_j.y = t'_j}. statement: Cover-rank lemma (L2, CLAIMED by this session, unreviewed). Let W = P + E over Q, rank(P) <= r, and suppose every nonzero entry of E lies in a row indexed by R or a column indexed by C. Then rank(W) <= r + |R| + |C|. Proof: let E_R be E with the rows outside R zeroed and E_C = E - E_R. The nonzero rows of E_R lie in R, so rank(E_R) <= |R|. Each nonzero entry of E_C lies outside R-rows, hence in a C-column, so rank(E_C) <= |C|. Subadditivity of rank gives rank(W) <= rank(P) + rank(E_R) + rank(E_C) <= r + |R| + |C|. The lemma is exact and general; its proof is four lines. Exact check: cm-085a13b0ab7343eb (2000 random instances, m,n <= 7, 0 failures, 594 tight equalities).

G0001(iii) (full rank) is untouched: for generic full-rank W the cover is C=all columns and the bound is vacuous. The DP corollary (rank-r DP, cm-2cd5c456ea174b3b) is a composition with the earlier CLAIMED rank-r lemma. label: S0123
statement: L3 (closed sign-pattern count, any dimension; repairs gap (f) of L2 without perturbation). Statement: for any d >= 0, m >= 0 and real affine functions f_1..f_m on R^d (f_j(x) = a_j.x - t_j, a_j = 0 allowed), the set P = { (1[f_j(x) >= 0])_{j<=m} : x in R^d } has |P| <= S(m,d) := sum_{i=0}^{d} C(m,i). PROOF by induction on m, all d at once. Base m=0: |P| = 1 = S(0,d). Base d=0: R^0 is one point, |P| <= 1 = S(m,0). Step m>=1, d>=1: let P' = patterns of f_1..f_{m-1} (the projection of P) and D = {p' in P' : both (p',0) and (p',1) lie in P}. Then |P| = |P'| + |D|. Case a_m = 0: f_m has constant sign, so D is empty and |P| = |P'| <= S(m-1,d) <= S(m,d). Case a_m != 0: H = {x : f_m(x) = 0} is an affine hyperplane isomorphic to R^{d-1}. Let p' in D be realised by x with f_m(x) >= 0 and y with f_m(y) < 0. Put z = (1-s)x + s y with s = f_m(x)/(f_m(x)-f_m(y)) in [0,1); then f_m(z) = 0, so z in H. Each f_j (j<m) is affine, so f_j(z) = (1-s) f_j(x) + s f_j(y). If p'_j = 1, both terms are >= 0, so f_j(z) >= 0; if p'_j = 0, both are < 0, so f_j(z) < 0. Hence z in H realises p' under the closed convention, so D lies in the pattern set of the m-1 restricted functions on H = R^{d-1}, and by induction |D| <= S(m-1,d-1). Therefore |P| <= S(m-1,d) + S(m-1,d-1) = S(m,d) by Pascal's rule C(m-1,i)+C(m-1,i-1) = C(m,i). QED. COROLLARY (rank r): if the bottom weights are W_j = U_j.A with U_j in Z^r and A an r x n integer matrix, then the bottom vector (1[W_j.x >= t_j])_j over x in {0,1}^n takes at most S(m,r) <= (m+1)^r values (subsets of [m] of size <= r inject into {0..m}^r by sorting and zero-padding). No general position, cell perturbation or half-open convention is needed, because the argument works with the closed sets directly. Numerical check: cm-5005f106b06d4a2d (exhaustive grid, m=2..5, coefficients and thresholds in {-1,0,1}; no violation).

label: S0129
statement: LEMMA L3 (sign-pattern bound, weight-free, rank r). Let W in Z^{m x n} have rank r over Q, t in Z^m, and for x in {0,1}^n put sigma(x)_j = [W_j . x >= t_j] in {0,1}^m. Then |{sigma(x) : x in {0,1}^n}| <= sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i). PROOF. Choose r linearly independent rows B of W; every row satisfies W_j = C_j B with C_j in Q^r. Put s = Bx in Z^r. Then W_j . x - t_j = C_j . s - t_j. Let D >= 1 be a common denominator of all C_j, so C_j . s - t_j lies in (1/D) Z for s in Z^r. Set tau_j = t_j - 1/(2D). Then C_j . s - tau_j lies in (1/D)Z + 1/(2D), which never equals 0, so sigma(x)_j = [C_j . s > tau_j] and no lattice point lies on any hyperplane H_j = {s : C_j . s = tau_j}. Hence sigma(x) is the sign vector of the cell of the affine arrangement {H_1..H_m} in R^r containing the point Bx. The number of cells of an arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r is at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) (Buck 1943 / Zaslavsky 1975; induction R(m,r) <= R(m-1,r) + R(m-1,r-1), R(0,r) = R(m,0) = 1, which solves to the sum). QED. SCOPE: any integer W of rank r, any integer thresholds, any n; no weight-size assumption. The bound counts distinct SIGN PATTERNS of the full input x. It is not a bound on the number of DP states of a prefix-by-prefix dynamic program, and it does not bound the number of residual functions of a prefix.

structure.gap: L3 does not close G0001(iii), G0006 or G0002. The DP state after a prefix is the prefix vector s_P = B_P x_P in Z^r. Its future behaviour is determined by the residual function x_S -> sign(C s_P + W_S x_S - t), not by the sign pattern of s_P alone. Counting residual classes needs the arrangement of m 2^{n-k} hyperplanes in R^r, which gives (m 2^{n-k})^r, not the Buck bound, so the saving does not follow. The table is consistent with the lemma: log2(sum C(m,r))/n at m = n^{1.5}, r = d n/log n tends to d/2 only slowly (0.92 at n = 4096, d = 1). Open: a residual-class bound for prefixes, which is G0005's clipped-state question.

label: S0227
statement:
statement_start: For integer-weight threshold-of-threshold circuits, merging prefixes with identical clipped signatures preserves the exact satisfying-assignment count.
statement: For C(x)=1[sum_j a_j y_j(x) >= T], with y_j(x)=1[sum_i w_ji x_i >= theta_j] and integer weights and thresholds, define a prefix signature at depth k by each bottom gate's status (forced 1, forced 0, or active), the exact partial sum for each active gate, and the top-level weighted sum of forced-1 gates. A gate is forced 1 when its partial sum plus the minimum possible remaining contribution is at least its threshold, and forced 0 when its partial sum plus the maximum possible remaining contribution is below its threshold. The dynamic program that extends prefixes by each next bit, recomputes statuses, merges equal signatures, and adds multiplicities returns the exact number of satisfying inputs.
proof: Induct on prefix length. The empty prefix is represented once. For an extension by bit b, add w_j,k+1*b to each active gate's partial sum and classify against the remaining suffix contributions. A previously forced gate remains forced to the same value because its new suffixes are a subset of the suffixes for which its value was already forced. If two prefixes have equal signatures, active gates have equal partial sums and hence equal outputs on every common suffix; forced gates have equal outputs by signature. Thus both prefixes induce the same circuit value for every common suffix. Merging them and summing multiplicities preserves the count of prefixes and all satisfying completions. At depth n all gate outputs are fixed, and accepting precisely when the resulting top-level weighted sum is at least T yields the exact count.

label: S0231
statement: statement: LEMMA (row-norm rank-after-deletion DP). Let W∈Z^{m×n}, C⊆[n], U=[n]\C, and let B_1,…,B_k be independent rows spanning the row space over Q of W[:,U]. Define L_l=Σ_{i∈U}|W_{B_l i}|. For f(x)=[Σ_j v_j[W_j·x≥t_j]≥T], #f is computable exactly in at most 2^{|C|}·poly(m,n)·∏_{l=1}^k(L_l+1) state-processing operations (arithmetic bit complexity additionally depends polynomially on input and intermediate bit lengths). Proof: Fix x_C. Process coordinates of x_U in any fixed order. At a prefix, store y_l=Σ_{i in prefix}W_{B_l i}x_i for each l, aggregating the number of prefixes at each vector y. Since x_i∈{0,1}, y_l lies between the sum of negative coefficients in that prefix and the sum of positive coefficients; hence it has at most 1+Σ_{i in prefix}|W_{B_l i}|≤L_l+1 possible integer values. Thus there are at most ∏_l(L_l+1) states at each layer, and the next-bit transition adds either zero or the next column vector. At the terminal layer each row W_j[:,U] is a rational linear combination of the spanning rows B_l, so W_j[:,U]·x_U is determined exactly by y. The fixed contribution W_j[:,C]·x_C is known, so every threshold gate and f is determined by the terminal state. Summing multiplicities of accepting terminal states counts all completions for this x_C; summing over all assignments x_C counts every x exactly once. There are |U|+1 layers and 2^{|C|} branches, giving the stated bound. If every selected basis row has coefficient absolute sum at most L, the state factor improves from (2a|U|+1)^k to (L+1)^k. This refines the state bound for the recorded rank-after-deletion gap; it does not imply a saving when these row norms or k are large.

label: S0233
statement: Repaired rank-after-deletion counting lemma. Let W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji|<=a, t,v in Z^m, T in Z, C a set of c columns, W'=W outside C, n'=n-c, and k=rank_Q(W'). Let L be total binary input length. The exact count of x in {0,1}^n satisfying sum_j v_j [W_j x>=t_j]>=T is computable in bit time 2^c(2an'+1)^k poly(m,n,L,log(2+a)). Proof: enumerate x_C. Choose k independent rows B_l of W'. Express every row W'_j as a rational combination of B_l using Cramer's rule on a nonsingular k-column minor. Hadamard's bound gives numerator and denominator bit lengths O(k log(2+a)+k log(2+n)). DP over remaining variables stores multiplicities by y=(B_l x_prefix)_l; each coordinate has at most 2an'+1 values. Each transition adds zero or one column vector and merges equal states. At the end each W'_j x is the same rational combination of y, so thresholds and the top gate are determined by y and x_C. Multiplicities are at most 2^n and have at most n+1 bits. Exact rational comparisons and additions cost polynomial in m,n,L,log(2+a) per transition. Summing accepting multiplicities over all 2^c branches proves the claim.
